definition_zh: 高地；高地区域；高地地带；山地牧场
definition_en: land that is higher than the country around it, especially a cool, hilly region used for grazing
core_image: 地面整体被抬高，形成一片起伏的草坡，风从坡顶掠过
scene: 云层贴着草坡移动，风比谷底冷得多。 Sheep graze on the highland above the village.
sceneCN: 此处指「高于周围、气候较冷的高处土地」（第 1 个义项：整体抬升的起伏地带）；句意为羊群在村子上方的高地上吃草。图中可辨识物件：贴坡移动的云、起伏草坡、羊群、谷底与高处的温差。

高地的（如 highland cattle、highland village）

senses.title: Land higher than its surroundings
senses.definition: ground that stands above the lower country around it
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围低地的地面
senses.example: Sheep graze on the highland above the village.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群在村子上方的高地上吃草。
senses.why: The compound is literal: high land. The defining feature is relative height, not rock or climate.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词是字面的：高的土地。定义特征是相对高度，而不是岩石或气候。

senses.title: A highland region in the plural
senses.definition: the highlands, used for a whole tract of elevated country
senses.definitionCN: 用复数指一整片抬高的地区
senses.example: Rain falls more heavily in the highlands.
senses.exampleCN: 高地区域的降雨更多。
senses.why: The plural turns elevated ground into a named region, the counterpart of the lowlands.
senses.whyCN: 复数把抬高的地面变成一个有名字的地区，与「低地」一词相对。

senses.title: The Scottish Highlands
senses.definition: the mountainous northern and western part of Scotland, with a distinct culture and history
senses.definitionCN: 苏格兰北部与西部的山地地区，有独特的文化与历史
senses.example: The Highlands are famous for deep valleys and bare ridges.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰高地以深谷与裸露山脊闻名。
senses.why: A capitalised proper name fixes the general word to one famous region.
senses.whyCN: 带大写的专名把这个一般词固定到一个著名的地区。

senses.title: A high-altitude ecological zone
senses.definition: the belt of land above the surrounding lowland, with cooler climate and different vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 位于周围低地之上、气候更冷、植被不同的地带
senses.example: Highland plants grow low to escape the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 高地植物贴地生长以躲避风。
senses.why: Ecology turns relative height into a measurable zone with its own species and climate.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把相对高度变成一个有自身物种与气候的可测量地带。

senses.title: Attributive: of the high country
senses.definition: used before a noun for the highland version of a thing, breed or place
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示某物、某品种或某地的高地类型
senses.example: Highland cattle have long hair and broad horns.
senses.exampleCN: 高地牛有长毛和宽角。
senses.why: The noun marks the altitude band where the following thing belongs.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词标出后面事物所属的海拔带。

senses.title: Hill pasture used for grazing
senses.definition: rough elevated grassland used for sheep or cattle in summer
senses.definitionCN: 夏季用来放羊或放牛的粗放高地草场
senses.example: The highland is open to grazing from May to October.
senses.exampleCN: 这片高地牧场从五月到十月开放放牧。
senses.why: People use the word for the land's economic role, not only its height.
senses.whyCN: 人们用这个词指土地的经济角色，而不只是它的高度。

senses.title: Highland people and culture
senses.definition: the communities and traditions of a highland region, contrasted with lowland society
senses.definitionCN: 高地地区的社群与传统，与低地社会相对
senses.example: Highland music travelled far beyond the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 高地音乐传到了群山之外很远的地方。
senses.why: A shared landscape produces shared customs, so the land word becomes a cultural label.
senses.whyCN: 共同的地貌产生共同的习俗，于是土地词变成文化标签。

senses.title: The highland side of a contrast
senses.definition: the elevated half of a regional highland-lowland division, used as a general concept
senses.definitionCN: 地区性高低二分中抬高的那一半，用作一般概念
senses.example: The highland and lowland economies depend on each other.
senses.exampleCN: 高地与低地经济彼此依赖。
senses.why: Once a region is divided by height, each half becomes a category that planners and historians can name.
senses.whyCN: 一片地区一旦按高度划分，每一半都成为规划者与历史学家可以命名的类别。

intro.en: Highland is a native English compound of high, from Old English hēah, and land. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: highland 是英语本族复合词，由来自古英语 hēah 的 high 与 land 组合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English hēah meant 'high, tall, exalted'; it is the native adjective behind modern high.
items.cn: 古英语 hēah 意为「高的、高大的、尊贵的」；它是现代 high 背后的本族形容词。

items.en: Old English land meant 'land, country, territory', a native Germanic word shared across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古英语 land 意为「土地、国家、领地」，是日耳曼语族共有的本土词。

items.en: Middle English high and land were both common; the compound highland appears later, when regional height contrasts needed a fixed term.
items.cn: 中古英语 high 与 land 都已常用；复合词 highland 出现较晚，是在地区高度对比需要固定说法之时。

items.en: The capitalised Highlands became the standard name for the Scottish uplands, especially after the eighteenth-century romantic interest in mountain scenery.
items.cn: 带大写的 Highlands 成为苏格兰高地的标准名称，尤其在 18 世纪对山地风景的浪漫兴趣兴起之后。

items.en: Modern geography uses highland as an altitude and relief class, often paired with lowland in regional descriptions.
items.cn: 现代地理学把 highland 用作海拔与起伏等级，常与 lowland 配对使用于区域描述。

items.en: Both elements are secure and native; only the first date of the compound is approximate. Neither element has a Latin etymon.
items.cn: 两个成分都可靠且为本族词，只有复合词的首见年代为约数。两个成分都没有拉丁词源。

note.en: The first group holds words built on high or land; the second holds words for elevated country.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 high 或 land 上的词；第二组是表示抬高地区的词。

entries.definition: Land lower than its surroundings; the direct height opposite, built the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 低于周围的地面；在高度上正相反，构词方式相同。

entries.definition: A person from a highland region; it adds -er to the same compound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自高地地区的人；是在同一复合词上加 -er。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'tall or elevated'; alone it describes height, not a region.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「高的、抬高的」形容词；单独使用时描述高度，而不是地区。

entries.definition: The plural of highland; it can also be a proper name for a specific region.
entries.definitionCN: highland 的复数；也可作为某一具体地区的专名。

entries.definition: Land higher than the nearby valleys; it is more neutral and less tied to a named region than highland.
entries.definitionCN: 高于附近谷地的土地；比 highland 更中性，也更少绑定某一具名地区。

entries.definition: A high area with a flat top; highland may be rolling, but a plateau specifically insists on flatness.
entries.definitionCN: 顶部平坦的高地；highland 可以是起伏的，而高原特别强调平坦。

entries.definition: Open rough upland, often peaty and wet; it adds vegetation and soil to the height.
entries.definitionCN: 开阔粗放的高地，常含泥炭且潮湿；它在高度之外加了植被与土壤。

entries.definition: A broad flat elevated region; it describes the shape directly, while highland describes relative position.
entries.definitionCN: 宽阔平坦的高地；直接描述形状，而 highland 描述相对位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two native elements, the real proper name and the altitude contrast with lowland.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个本族成分、真实的专名，以及与 lowland 的海拔对比。

normal.en: high + land: literally 'high land'.
normal.cn: high + land：字面就是「高的土地」。

normal.en: The family runs highland, highlands, highlander, highland cattle, highland fling.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 highland、highlands、highlander、highland cattle、highland fling。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: highland area, highland region, highland village, highland climate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 highland area、highland region、highland village、highland climate。

normal.en: Lowland is the mirror compound: same structure, opposite height.
normal.cn: lowland 是镜像复合词：结构相同，高度相反。

normal.en: The Highlands capitalises the word for Scotland's uplands.
normal.cn: The Highlands 用大写把这个词固定为苏格兰高地。

abstract.en: Picture a green blanket lifted at one end so that it slopes upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿色毯子一端被提起，于是向上倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture clouds dragging along a slope instead of floating above it.
abstract.cn: 想象云层沿着坡面拖行，而不是飘在上方。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of the same country, one shaded brown at the top and one green at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个国家的两张地图，一张顶部染褐，一张底部染绿。

examples.en: The highland receives more rain than the coast.
examples.cn: 高地比海岸得到更多降雨。

examples.en: Highland roads close when snow blocks the passes.
examples.cn: 大雪封住山口时，高地公路会封闭。

examples.en: Many Highlanders left for the cities in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 19 世纪，许多高地居民迁往城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨（hai）+ 兰（lan）+ 的（d）」—— 嗨到高处的草地，风大又冷 → 高地

root: high（古英语 hēah「高的」）+ land（古英语 land「土地」）→ 字面「高的土地」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with ground above its surroundings, then extend to a region, a famous proper name, an ecological belt, a habitat label, pasture, a culture and one half of a regional contrast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「高于周围的地面」出发，再扩展到一片地区、一个著名专名、一条生态带、一类生境、牧场、一种文化，以及地区对比中的一半。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rolling surface lifted above the valleys, colder and windier than the ground below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片被抬到谷地之上的起伏地面，比下方更冷、风更大。

branches.en: THE GROUND: a raised stretch, and the plural that makes it a region.
branches.cn: 土地：一段抬高的地面，以及把它变成地区的复数。

branches.en: THE NAME: the Highlands fixes the word to Scotland's uplands.
branches.cn: 名称：The Highlands 把这个词固定为苏格兰高地。

branches.en: THE BELT: altitude creates a zone with its own plants, breeds and weather.
branches.cn: 地带：海拔造出一个拥有自身植物、品种与天气的区域。

branches.en: THE PASTURE: the land's use as summer grazing.
branches.cn: 牧场：这片土地作为夏季放牧之用的角色。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THE DIVISION: shared height makes shared culture and a regional half.
branches.cn: 人与划分：共同的高度造就共同的文化，也构成地区的一半。

intro.en: Highland is a transparent native compound; its family comes from the two elements and from names of highland breeds, dances and places.
intro.cn: highland 是透明的本族复合词；词族来自两个成分，以及高地品种、舞蹈与地名。

latinIntro.en: Neither element has a Latin etymon: high is native Old English hēah and land is Old English land, so the Latin entry list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都没有拉丁词源：high 是古英语本族词 hēah，land 是古英语 land，因此拉丁条目按规则留空。

items.example: The wall is two metres high.
The land rises toward the north.
The highland is cool even in summer.
The highlands feed the main rivers.
items.exampleCN: 高地区域为主要的河流供水。
一位高地居民给队伍带路。

items.meaning: a hardy breed with long hair

items.meaningCN: 一种活泼的苏格兰独舞
items.example: The highland fling ends the evening.
items.exampleCN: 高地弗林舞为夜晚收尾。

items.meaning: the cooler, wetter climate of high ground

items.example: The road drops from highland to lowland.
items.exampleCN: 公路从高地下降到低地。

definition_zh: adj. 可以达到的；能够获得的（目标、水平、结果）
definition_en: Able to be reached, achieved or obtained, especially of a goal or standard that is realistic.
core_image: 伸手就能碰到的那根横杆
scene: 教练把跳高横杆降到学生平时能过的高度，说这样目标才有意义。 The coach lowered the bar to a height that was attainable for every student.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attainable 指目标在能力范围之内，努力之后确实能够达到。

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: A goal within reach
senses.definition: of an aim, level or result that a person can realistically reach with effort
senses.definitionCN: 指目标、水平或结果在努力之后确实能够达到
senses.example: She set an attainable target of ten pages a day.
senses.exampleCN: 她定了每天十页这个可达成的目标。
senses.why: The word joins attain, to reach, with -able, capable of, so it literally means reachable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 attain「达到」加 -able「能够……的」构成，字面就是「可达到的」。

senses.title: Available to be obtained
senses.definition: of a resource, status or benefit that can actually be got or secured
senses.definitionCN: 指资源、地位或利益实际上可以取得或获得
senses.example: Free childcare is attainable only in a few districts.
senses.exampleCN: 免费托育只在少数几个区才能获得。
senses.why: Once reaching a height was clear, the same suffix pattern covered getting hold of anything desired.
senses.whyCN: 「达到某个高度」清楚之后，同一后缀模式也覆盖了「取得任何想要的东西」。

intro.en: Attainable is attain plus -able; attain comes from Old French ataindre, from Latin attingere, to touch upon, from ad-, to, and tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: attainable 是 attain 加 -able；attain 来自古法语 ataindre，出自拉丁语 attingere「触及」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成。

items.en: The root tag- meant to touch, the physical act behind a whole family of contact words.
items.cn: 词根 tag- 意为「触碰」，是一整族接触类词背后的身体动作。

items.en: Latin tangere meant to touch, giving tangent, contact and contingent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tangere 意为「触」，产生 tangent、contact 与 contingent。

items.en: With ad-, to, added, attingere meant to touch upon, to reach as far as a point.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」，attingere 意为「触及」，即延伸到某一点。

items.en: Old French ataindre kept the sense of reaching a place or a person.
items.cn: 古法语 ataindre 保留了「抵达某地或某人」的意思。

items.en: Middle English atteynen meant to reach or arrive at, later spelled attain.
items.cn: 中古英语 atteynen 意为「达到、抵达」，后来拼作 attain。

items.en: English added -able in the sixteenth century to say that a goal could be reached.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪加上 -able，用来表示某个目标能够达到。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the attain family and one familiar -able word; the near-meaning group lists other words for a goal that can be met.
note.cn: 形近组保留 attain 词族和一个常见的 -able 词；近义组列出其他表示目标能够达成的词。

entries.definition: To reach or achieve something.
entries.definitionCN: 达到或取得某物。

entries.definition: Impossible to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 不可能达到的。

entries.definition: The quality of being reachable.
entries.definitionCN: 可达到的性质。

entries.definition: Able to be kept up over time.
entries.definitionCN: 能长期维持的。

entries.definition: Able to be accomplished.
entries.definitionCN: 能够完成的。

entries.definition: Possible to do in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 实际可行的。

entries.definition: Sensible given the limits.
entries.definitionCN: 在限制之下合理的。

entries.definition: Able to be got to.
entries.definitionCN: 能够到达的。

normalIntro.en: Attainable splits into attain plus -able: if you can attain it, it is attainable.
normalIntro.cn: attainable 拆成 attain 加 -able：能达到的，就是 attainable。

normal.en: Attain means reach; -able means can be.
normal.cn: attain 意为达到，-able 意为「可以被」。

normal.en: The opposite adds un-: unattainable.
normal.cn: 反义加 un- 就成 unattainable。

normal.en: Goals should be challenging yet attainable.
normal.cn: 目标应当有挑战但仍可达成。

normal.en: The noun is attainability, not attainableness.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 attainability，不用 attainableness。

normal.en: It usually sits before goal, target or standard.
normal.cn: 它通常放在 goal、target 或 standard 之前。

abstract.en: Picture a high-jump bar set at your own height.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高横杆设在你自己能够的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine a shelf just within your fingertips.
abstract.cn: 想象一层刚好在指尖之内的架子。

abstract.en: Think of a plan whose last step is possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一份最后一步确实可行的计划。

examples.en: The salary is attainable after two years.
examples.cn: 两年后这份薪水是可以拿到的。

examples.en: Make the first milestone easily attainable.
examples.cn: 把第一个里程碑定得容易达到。

examples.en: Such purity is not attainable at home.
examples.cn: 这样的纯度在家无法达到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：attain「达到」+ -able「可以……的」——能够达到的，就是 attainable。

root: 拉丁语 tangere「触」加 ad-「向」成 attingere「触及」，经古法语 ataindre 入英语作 attain「达到」；再加 -able 表「可以被达到」，即 attainable。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same reach: a height you can get to, and a thing you can get hold of.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种「够得到」：能达到的高度，以及能拿到手的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar set just within the reach of your hand
core.cn: 核心意象：横杆设在伸手就能碰到的高度

branches.en: A daily page target one can meet.
branches.cn: 能完成的每日页数目标。

branches.en: A bar lowered to a reachable height.
branches.cn: 降到可及高度的横杆。

branches.en: Free childcare only in a few districts.
branches.cn: 只在少数区能获得的免费托育。

branches.en: A salary one can earn in two years.
branches.cn: 两年内能挣到的薪水。

branches.en: Both stay inside real limits.
branches.cn: 两者都在现实限制之内。

intro.en: Attainable is at- plus tain plus -able; the same tain root builds contain, retain and maintain.
intro.cn: attainable 是 at- 加 tain 加 -able；同一 tain 词根还构成 contain、retain 与 maintain。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tangere, to touch, and attingere, to touch upon; tenere, to hold, gives the look-alike tain family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tangere「触」与 attingere「触及」；tenere「持」则给出形近的 tain 词族。

definition_zh: 生态足迹；维持某一人群或活动所需的生物生产性土地与水域面积
definition_en: the area of productive land and water needed to supply a population's resources and absorb its wastes
core_image: 沙地上留下一个清晰脚印，旁边并排展开草地、农田、水域与林地的面积刻度
scene: 沙地上留下一个清晰脚印，旁边并排画出草地、农田、水域与林地的面积。 The report measured the ecological footprint of the whole city.
sceneCN: 这里 ecological footprint 指「维持某群体所需的生产性土地与水域面积」（第 1 个义项：把资源消耗与废物吸收折算成土地面积）；句意为报告测量了整座城市的生态足迹。图中可辨识物件：脚印、田块、水域、林地边界。

pos.zh: 生态足迹（可数；复数 ecological footprints）

derivatives.zh: 足迹；影响范围
生态的
生态学；生态系统
生态学家

senses.title: The land area a population requires
senses.titleCN: 某群体所需的土地面积
senses.definition: the productive land and water area required to supply a group's resources and absorb its waste
senses.definitionCN: 为一个群体提供资源并吸收其废物所需的生产性土地与水域面积
senses.example: The report measured the ecological footprint of the whole city.
senses.exampleCN: 报告测量了整座城市的生态足迹。
senses.why: footprint names the mark left by standing on land, and ecological names the living system; together they say how much land a way of life occupies.
senses.whyCN: footprint 指踩在土地上留下的印记，ecological 指生命系统；合起来表示一种生活方式占用了多少土地。

senses.title: A per-capita or national indicator
senses.titleCN: 人均或国家层面的指标
senses.definition: the figure expressed per person or per country for comparison across populations
senses.definitionCN: 按人均或按国家表达的数值，用于比较不同人群
senses.example: The atlas lists the ecological footprint of every nation.
senses.exampleCN: 这本图集列出了每个国家的生态足迹。
senses.why: an area becomes an indicator once it is divided by population and put into a table.
senses.whyCN: 当面积被人口相除并放进表格，它就变成了指标。

senses.title: The carbon component
senses.definition: the share of the footprint that represents land needed to absorb carbon dioxide
senses.definitionCN: 足迹中代表吸收二氧化碳所需土地的那一部分
senses.example: Flying added a large block to her ecological footprint.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行给她的生态足迹增加了一大块。
senses.why: waste absorption needs land too, and carbon is the waste that dominates modern accounts.
senses.whyCN: 吸收废物同样需要土地，而碳是现代核算中占主导的废物。

senses.title: A formal accounting method
senses.definition: the method that converts consumption and waste into global hectares for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 把消费与废物折算成全球公顷以便比较的方法
senses.example: The course teaches ecological footprint accounting step by step.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课逐步讲授生态足迹核算。
senses.why: once the idea is given a unit and a procedure, the phrase also names the method rather than only the result.
senses.whyCN: 当这个想法有了单位与程序，短语也就指方法，而不只是结果。

senses.title: A corporate or product label
senses.definition: the footprint attributed to a firm, a supply chain or a single product
senses.definitionCN: 归属于某公司、供应链或单一产品的足迹
senses.example: The label printed the ecological footprint of the shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上印着这件衬衫的生态足迹。
senses.why: firms shrink the population to a product so that buyers can compare one purchase with another.
senses.whyCN: 企业把群体缩小为一件产品，好让购买者比较不同商品。

senses.title: An urban planning metric
senses.definition: a measure used to test whether a district's land use fits within its region
senses.definitionCN: 用来检验某街区土地利用是否落在本区域承载范围内的量度
senses.example: Planners compared the district's ecological footprint with its hinterland.
senses.exampleCN: 规划者把该街区的生态足迹与其腹地作比较。
senses.why: cities import their land use from elsewhere, so the metric makes that hidden dependence visible.
senses.whyCN: 城市从别处输入土地利用，这个指标让这种隐藏的依赖变得可见。

senses.title: The sign of planetary overshoot
senses.definition: a symbol for demand exceeding the planet's regenerative capacity
senses.definitionCN: 象征需求超过地球再生能力的标志
senses.example: Earth overshoot day is the ecological footprint made into a calendar date.
senses.exampleCN: 地球超载日就是把生态足迹变成日历上的一个日期。
senses.why: when footprints are added up, they can be compared with the total land available, and the gap reads as overshoot.
senses.whyCN: 把足迹相加后，可与可用土地总量比较，差额就被读作超载。

senses.title: Any trace left on a system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：留在系统上的任何痕迹
senses.definition: the total disturbance any activity leaves on a system that must absorb it
senses.definitionCN: 任何活动在一个必须吸收它的系统上留下的总扰动
senses.example: The studio measured its ecological footprint in server hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室用服务器小时来衡量自己的生态足迹。
senses.why: the metaphor survives wherever an activity draws on a finite pool and returns a residue.
senses.whyCN: 只要一项活动取用有限资源并留下残余，这个比喻就成立。

intro.en: Ecological footprint joins Greek oikos 'house' and -logia 'study' to the native English words foot and print. The phrase was coined at the end of the twentieth century as an accounting tool. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ecological footprint 把希腊 oikos「家」与 -logia「研究」接到英语本族的 foot 与 print 上。这个短语在 20 世纪末作为一种核算工具被造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, household, family property'. Ecology later took it as the root for the whole household of nature.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、家庭、家产」。生态学后来把它当作整个自然之家的词根。

items.en: -Logia 'study of' comes from logos 'word, reason, account'. Ecology was coined in 1866 as the study of the household of nature.
items.cn: -logia「…研究」来自 logos「言词、理性、账目」。ecology 于 1866 年被造出，指研究自然之家的学问。

items.en: Fot 'foot' is a native Germanic word. Print came through Old French preinte from Latin premere 'to press'.
items.cn: fot「脚」是日耳曼本族词。print 经古法语 preinte 来自拉丁 premere「压」。

items.en: Footprint first meant the mark of a foot on ground or snow; the extended sense of the area something occupies is much later.
items.cn: footprint 最初指脚在地面或雪上留下的印子；表示某物占用面积的引申义出现得晚得多。

items.en: Ecological footprint was coined in the early 1990s as a way to express resource demand in hectares of land.
items.cn: ecological footprint 于 1990 年代初被造出，用土地公顷来表达资源需求。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek origin of oikos is unsettled, and the exact first printed use of the phrase is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：oikos 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，这个短语确切的最早书证也没有定说。

note.en: Group one holds footprint compounds that are often substituted for this phrase; group two holds the accounting concepts it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是常被用来替换本短语的 footprint 复合词；第二组是与之相比较的核算概念。

entries.definition: The part of the account that covers greenhouse gases only; the ecological footprint also counts food, fibre and built land.
entries.definitionCN: 只覆盖温室气体的那一部分；生态足迹还计入食物、纤维与建设用地。

entries.definition: The volume of fresh water used by a product or group, measured in litres rather than hectares.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或群体使用的淡水量，以升而非公顷计量。

entries.definition: A broad label for any environmental impact, often without the strict land-area method.
entries.definitionCN: 对任何环境影响的宽泛标签，通常不含严格的土地面积算法。

entries.definition: The mark of a foot; used alone it can also mean the physical space a machine occupies.
entries.definitionCN: 脚留下的印子；单独使用时也可指机器占用的物理空间。

entries.tag: the other side of the ratio
entries.definition: The land's ability to supply resources and absorb waste; the footprint is demand against this supply.
entries.definitionCN: 土地提供资源并吸收废物的能力；足迹是相对这一供给的需求。

entries.definition: The maximum population an area can support; it is a limit, while the footprint is a measured demand.
entries.definitionCN: 某区域能支撑的最大种群；它是上限，而足迹是测得的需求。

entries.definition: The amount by which demand passes capacity; the footprint is the measure that reveals it.
entries.definitionCN: 需求超出承载力的部分；足迹是揭示它的量度。

entries.definition: The state of living within capacity; the footprint is one tool for testing whether that state is reached.
entries.definitionCN: 在承载范围内生活的状态；足迹是检验是否达到该状态的一种工具。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oikos 'house' + logos 'account': ecology is the accounting of nature's household.
normal.cn: oikos「家」+ logos「账目」：生态学就是对自然之家的记账。

normal.en: foot + print: the phrase asks how much ground a lifestyle stands on.
normal.cn: foot + print：这个短语问的是一种生活方式占了多少地。

normal.en: The family runs ecology, ecological, ecologist, footprint, environmental footprint.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 ecology、ecological、ecologist、footprint、environmental footprint。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the method: ecological footprint analysis, per capita ecological footprint.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方法：生态足迹分析、人均生态足迹。

normal.en: Biocapacity is the supply side; the footprint is the demand side of the same ledger.
normal.cn: 生物承载力是供给方，生态足迹是同一账本的需求方。

abstract.en: Picture a footprint so large that the ground beneath it must be imported.
abstract.cn: 想象一个脚印大到它脚下的土地必须靠进口。

abstract.en: Picture a household whose rubbish pile is taller than its garden.
abstract.cn: 想象一户人家，垃圾堆比自家花园还高。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt that lists land instead of money.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小票，上面列的是土地而不是钱。

examples.en: Beef raises a household's ecological footprint more than beans do.
examples.cn: 牛肉比豆类更能抬高一个家庭的生态足迹。

examples.en: The class calculated its ecological footprint from food and travel data.
examples.cn: 全班根据饮食与出行数据计算了自己的生态足迹。

examples.en: A city's ecological footprint often exceeds its own borders.
examples.cn: 一座城市的生态足迹常常超出它自己的边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ecological（生态的）+ footprint（脚印）」——生活方式在地球上踩出的脚印 → 生态足迹

root: 希腊 oikos「家」+ -logia「研究」（来自 logos「账目、理性」）构成 ecology/ecological；footprint 为英语本族 foot 加经古法语来自拉丁 premere「压」的 print。整个短语是 20 世纪末的核算造词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ledger: resources are taken, waste is returned, both are converted into land area, and that area is then read per person, split into carbon, turned into a method, attached to products, mapped onto cities, summed into overshoot and finally borrowed as a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一本账展开：取用资源、排出废物、两者折算为土地面积，随后这个面积按人均读出、拆出碳部分、变成方法、贴到产品上、映射到城市、汇总为超载，最后被借作比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a footprint beside a measured patch of field, water and forest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个脚印旁边是被丈量过的农田、水域与林地。

branches.en: LAND ACCOUNTING: the base measure is the area a group or district needs, wherever that land lies.
branches.cn: 土地核算：基本量度是一个群体或街区所需的面积，无论那片土地在哪里。

branches.en: INDICATOR AND CARBON: the area is divided per person, and one block of it is carbon absorption.
branches.cn: 指标与碳：面积按人均相除，其中一块是碳吸收。

branches.en: METHOD AND LABEL: the procedure becomes a formal analysis and is then printed on products.
branches.cn: 方法与标签：程序成为正式分析，随后印到产品上。

branches.en: OVERSHOOT: total demand compared with total capacity produces the calendar symbol of Earth overshoot day.
branches.cn: 超载：总需求与总承载力相比，产生地球超载日这一日历象征。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any activity that draws on a finite pool and leaves a residue can be given a footprint.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何取用有限资源并留下残余的活动都可以被赋予足迹。

intro.en: Ecological footprint is a hybrid phrase: Greek elements form the adjective, native Germanic and French elements form the noun. Each part remains productive in modern English.
intro.cn: ecological footprint 是一个混合短语：希腊成分构成形容词，日耳曼本族成分与法语成分构成名词。每一部分在现代英语中仍有构词能力。

latinIntro.en: Neo-Latin oecologia transmits the Greek oikos to English; Latin premere 'to press' gives print, imprint and impress.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁 oecologia 把希腊 oikos 传给英语；拉丁 premere「压」衍生 print、imprint 与 impress。

intro.en: Emission comes from Latin e- meaning out and mittere meaning to send; emittere is to send out, and the noun names both the sending and what is sent.
intro.cn: emission 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 mittere（送）；emittere 意为送出，名词既指送出的动作，也指被送出的东西。

items.en: Mittere means to send, and gives English mission, transmit and permit.
items.cn: mittere 意为送，给出英语 mission、transmit 与 permit。

items.en: Emittere means to send out, built from e- plus mittere.
items.cn: emittere 意为送出，由 e- 加 mittere 构成。

items.en: Emissio is the noun of action, meaning a sending out.

items.en: Physics uses emission for the lines a hot gas gives out.

items.en: Climate policy makes emissions a countable thing to be cut.

dict_mnemonic.text: emission ＝ e-（向外）＋ miss（送，拉丁 mittere，过去分词 missus）＋ -ion（名词后缀）＝「送出去这件事」。动词 emit 发出、排放，名词 emitter 发射体、排放源，形容词 emissive 发射的；同根 mission 使命、transmit 传送、permit 允许、omission 遗漏、emissary 使者。三类用法：动作 the emission of light 光的发射；数量 carbon emissions 碳排放、cut vehicle emissions 削减汽车尾气；信号与发行 first emission of banknotes 纸币的首次发行。常见搭配 emission standards 排放标准、zero emission 零排放、greenhouse gas emissions 温室气体排放。可数：an emission 一次排放，emissions 多笔排放。注意与 omission（遗漏）只差一个字母，与 commission（委员会；佣金）同根不同缀。

sub-（在下）+ mergere（拉丁「沉入」）+ -sion（名词后缀）→ 浸没、下潜：沉入水下的动作或状态

senses.title: A diving warship
senses.definition: a vessel designed to operate beneath the surface
senses.definitionCN: 设计为在水面之下运作的船只
senses.example: The submarine dived quietly beside the research ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘潜艇在考察船旁悄然下潜。
senses.why: sub- 'under' plus marinus 'of the sea' literally means 'undersea', and the noun applies that to a craft.
senses.whyCN: sub-「在下」加 marinus「海的」字面就是「海下」，名词把这个意思用在船只上。

senses.title: The submarine force
senses.definition: the branch of a navy that operates submarines, or its crews
senses.definitionCN: 海军中运作潜艇的兵种，或指其艇员
senses.example: Submarine crews train for months before deployment.
senses.exampleCN: 潜艇艇员在部署前训练数月。
senses.why: a fleet branch is named by its main equipment, so the word also stands for the service.
senses.whyCN: 兵种常以主要装备命名，因此这个词也代表该兵种。

senses.title: Beneath the sea, as an adjective
senses.definition: existing or occurring below the sea surface
senses.definitionCN: 存在于海面之下或发生在海面之下
senses.example: Submarine cables carry most international internet traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 海底电缆承载大部分国际互联网流量。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the literal sense of the Latin parts and attaches to whatever lies under the sea.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留拉丁成分的字面义，附在任何位于海面之下的事物上。

senses.title: Seafloor geology
senses.definition: the adjective used for canyons, fans and ridges on the seafloor
senses.definitionCN: 用于海床上的峡谷、扇体与洋脊的形容词
senses.example: The submarine canyon feeds a fan of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这条海底峡谷养出一片砂质扇体。
senses.why: geology needed a short modifier for features hidden under water, and reused the existing adjective.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要一个简短限定词来指藏在海水之下的地貌，于是复用了现成的形容词。

senses.title: Submarine cable engineering
senses.definition: the adjective for cables, pipes and structures laid on the seabed
senses.definitionCN: 用于铺设在海床上的电缆、管道与结构的形容词
senses.example: A submarine cable links the island to the mainland.
senses.exampleCN: 一条海底电缆把该岛与大陆相连。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrowed the adjective to installed infrastructure rather than ships.
senses.whyCN: 工程义把这个形容词收窄到已安装的基础设施，而非船只。

senses.title: The long sandwich
senses.titleCN: 潜艇三明治：长条夹心面包
senses.definition: a long roll split and filled, named for its shape
senses.definitionCN: 剖开夹馅的长条面包，因形状得名
senses.example: He ordered a submarine with cheese and ham.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一份夹奶酪与火腿的潜艇三明治。
senses.why: a long filled roll resembles a hull, so American English borrowed the vessel's name for the food.
senses.whyCN: 长条夹馅面包形似艇体，因此美式英语借船名来称这种食物。

senses.title: The underhand pitch
senses.definition: a baseball pitch delivered with the arm below the shoulder
senses.definitionCN: 手臂低于肩部投出的棒球球路
senses.example: The reliever throws with a submarine motion.
senses.exampleCN: 这名后援投手以下手动作投球。
senses.why: the low arm slot is figuratively beneath the usual plane, so baseball borrowed the sea word.
senses.whyCN: 低臂位在通常平面之下，因此棒球借用了这个海词。

senses.title: Hidden and silent action
senses.definition: the quality of moving unseen and unheard, as a submarine does
senses.definitionCN: 像潜艇那样不被看见、不被听见地行动
senses.example: The campaign ran like a submarine, silent until it surfaced.
senses.exampleCN: 这场行动像潜艇一样，一直无声，直到浮出水面。
senses.why: a submarine's military value is invisibility, so the word became a metaphor for concealed action.
senses.whyCN: 潜艇的军事价值在于不可见，因此这个词成为隐蔽行动的隐喻。

intro.en: Submarine is Latin in its parts: sub- 'under' plus marinus 'of the sea', from mare 'sea'. It entered English as an adjective in the seventeenth century and became a noun for the vessel at the end of the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: submarine 的各成分都是拉丁语：sub-「在下」加 marinus「海的」，后者来自 mare「海」。它于十七世纪以形容词进入英语，到十九世纪末成为指舰船的名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant 'under, below' and is the prefix in submerge, subsoil and submarine.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，是 submerge、subsoil 与 submarine 的前缀。

items.en: Mare 'sea' produced marinus 'of the sea', the source of the -marine part.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，即 -marine 部分的来源。

items.en: Submarine first described things living or lying beneath the sea, not ships.
items.cn: submarine 最初描述生活在海面之下或位于海面之下的事物，并非船只。

items.en: Experimental submarines appeared in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, but the noun submarine for a warship settled in English around 1900.
items.cn: 实验性潜水器在十七、十八世纪出现，但指军舰的名词 submarine 约于一九零零年在英语中定型。

items.en: Two world wars made submarine a common word for the warship, and engineering extended it to cables and geology.
items.cn: 两次世界大战使 submarine 成为军舰的常用词，工程又把它扩展到电缆与地质。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): dates for the first noun use vary between 1899 and the early 1900s, and no single citation is universally accepted.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：名词首次使用的年代在各家著作中自一八九九年至二十世纪初不等，没有公认的唯一书证。

note.en: Group one holds the vessels and craft most often confused with a submarine; group two holds the adjectives for things beneath the sea.
note.cn: 第一组是常与潜艇混淆的船只与潜器；第二组是表示海面之下的形容词。

entries.definition: A small craft carried by a ship and used for research or repair; it usually has no long-range independent patrol.
entries.definitionCN: 由母船携带、用于研究或修理的小型潜器；通常不能独立远航巡逻。

entries.definition: A person who works or swims underwater; it is human, not a vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 在水下工作或游泳的人；是人，不是船。

entries.definition: Any naval vessel built for combat; a submarine is one kind of warship, not the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 任何为作战建造的海军舰船；潜艇是军舰的一种，不是总称。

entries.definition: A long filled roll named for its hull-like shape; it has no connection to naval vessels beyond the metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 因形似艇体而得名的长条夹馅面包；除比喻外与军舰无关。

entries.definition: Beneath the sea, used of the seabed and its features; it is an adjective and cannot name the vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 海面之下，用于海床及其地貌；只是形容词，不能命名舰船。

entries.definition: Below the surface of any water, fresh or salt; it is broader and not naval.
entries.definitionCN: 任何水体表面之下，淡水或咸水；范围更宽，且非海军用语。

entries.definition: Living or occurring partly under water; it is biological and rare, not a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 部分在水下生活或发生的；属生物学用语且罕见，不指船只。

entries.definition: Covered by water, often after sinking; a submarine is submerged by design, but the adjective alone implies no crew or engine.
entries.definitionCN: 被水覆盖，常因沉没；潜艇是设计上被淹没，但单用该形容词不暗示船员或动力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin parts, real naval and technical compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分、真实的海军与技术复合词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sub means under, mare means sea: the boat and the adjective say the same thing.
normal.cn: sub 是在下，mare 是海：船与形容词说的是同一件事。

normal.en: The adjective came first, the vessel noun came last: 1620s then about 1900.
normal.cn: 形容词先来，船只名词后到：十七世纪二十年代，再到约一九零零年。

normal.en: Fixed compounds split the senses: submarine cable is engineering, submarine canyon is geology.
normal.cn: 固定复合词分开义项：submarine cable 是工程，submarine canyon 是地质。

normal.en: The sandwich is named by shape, not by navy: a long roll like a hull.
normal.cn: 三明治按形状得名，与海军无关：长条面包像艇体。

normal.en: A submarine's weapon is silence: it is dangerous because it cannot be seen.
normal.cn: 潜艇的武器是沉默：它危险正因为看不见。

abstract.en: A submarine is a room that agrees to be forgotten.
abstract.cn: 潜艇是一间同意被遗忘的房间。

abstract.en: It moves through the sea the way a thought moves through silence.
abstract.cn: 它在海里移动，像念头在沉默中移动。

abstract.en: Its power is not speed but the absence of a surface.
abstract.cn: 它的力量不在速度，而在于没有表面。

examples.en: The submarine surfaced after a sixty-day patrol.
examples.cn: 这艘潜艇在六十天巡逻后浮出水面。

examples.en: Submarine cables carry data across the Atlantic.
examples.cn: 海底电缆跨大西洋传输数据。

examples.en: The museum displays a submarine from the last century.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出一艘上个世纪的潜艇。

dict_mnemonic.text: sub（在下）+ marine（海的）＝海面之下的；作名词就是潜艇，作形容词用于海底电缆、海底峡谷。

root: 拉丁 sub-「在下」+ marinus「海的」（源自 mare「海」）；十七世纪作形容词，十九世纪末作潜艇名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one craft and one position: the vessel, its service, the undersea adjective, seafloor geology, cables, the sandwich, the low pitch and the metaphor of silent concealment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一艘船与一个位置展开：舰艇、兵种、海下形容词、海底地质、电缆、三明治、低手投球，以及无声隐蔽的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long dark hull sliding under the surface until only a periscope remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：细长的深色艇体滑入水下，只剩潜望镜露在外面。

branches.en: CRAFT AND SERVICE: the vessel itself, then the branch that sails it.
branches.cn: 船与兵种：先是舰艇本身，再是运作它的兵种。

branches.en: THE UNDERSEA ADJECTIVE: position, seafloor geology, installed infrastructure.
branches.cn: 海下形容词：位置、海底地质、已安装设施。

branches.en: SHAPE METAPHOR: a long roll borrows the hull's name.
branches.cn: 形状比喻：长条面包借用了艇体的名字。

branches.en: LOW ARM SLOT: the pitch comes from beneath the usual plane.
branches.cn: 低臂位：球从通常平面之下投出。

branches.en: SILENT CONCEALMENT: invisibility becomes the point of the word.
branches.cn: 无声隐蔽：不可见成为这个词的要点。

intro.en: Submarine is a Latin prefix plus a Latin adjective, both still readable, and the English word inherits the full morphological structure.
intro.cn: submarine 是拉丁前缀加拉丁形容词，两者至今可读，英语词继承了完整的构词结构。

latinIntro.en: Sub- and marinus are the Latin entries; mare is the noun behind marinus. Together they spell 'under the sea'.
latinIntro.cn: sub- 与 marinus 是拉丁条目；mare 是 marinus 背后的名词。二者合起来就是「海之下」。

definition_zh: 天真的；不狡诈的；笨拙的；缺乏技巧的
definition_en: without cunning or deceit; natural and simple, or lacking skill and craft
core_image: 一张不会说谎的脸：话直来直去，不设防备
scene: 小女孩把自己画的歪歪扭扭的小猫送给祖母，眼睛里没有一丝算计。 The girl gave her grandmother the crooked cat she had drawn with an artless smile.
sceneCN: 这里 artless 是「天真无邪的、不做作的」（第 1 个义项：没有机心）；句意是女孩带着天真的笑容送出歪歪扭扭的画。

pos.zh: 天真的；不狡诈的；朴实的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「天真地；笨拙地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「天真；质朴」
反义构词（artful），义为「狡猾的；巧妙欺人的」

senses.title: Without deceit or cunning
senses.definition: free from deception or trickery; honest in a natural, childlike way
senses.definitionCN: 毫无欺骗或诡计，以自然的、孩子般的方式坦率诚实
senses.example: Her artless questions disarmed the interviewer.
senses.exampleCN: 她天真直率的问题让面试官卸下了防备。
senses.why: The suffix -less means without, and art here once meant cunning or craft, so artless literally means without cunning.
senses.whyCN: -less 表示「没有」，而 art 在古义中指「诡计、技巧」，字面即「无机心的」。

senses.title: Unintentionally natural
senses.definition: unaffected and spontaneous, without careful design
senses.definitionCN: 不做作、自然流露，未经刻意设计
senses.example: The poem has an artless beauty that feels unpolished yet sincere.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗有一种不加雕饰的美，看似未经打磨却真诚动人。
senses.why: Because cunning craft is absent, what remains is plainness, which becomes a virtue in style or manner.
senses.whyCN: 既然没有机巧，剩下的就是朴素，在风格上反而成为美德。

senses.title: Lacking skill
senses.definition: showing little skill, cleverness, or effectiveness
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏技巧、灵巧或成效
senses.example: The thief's artless attempt to pick the lock was caught on camera.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷蹩脚的开锁尝试全被摄像头拍了下来。
senses.why: If art means skill, then having no art means doing something clumsily and badly.
senses.whyCN: 如果 art 指「技艺」，那么「没有 art」就是做得笨拙糟糕。

intro.en: Artless is formed from art in its older sense of skill, craft, or cunning, plus the negative suffix -less.
intro.cn: artless 由 art 的古义「技艺、巧计」加否定后缀 -less 构成，字面即「无机巧的」。

items.en: Latin ars, artis means skill, craft, or method.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ars（属格 artis）意为技艺、手艺、方法。

items.en: Old French art carried the senses of skill and also of cunning.
items.cn: 古法语 art 兼有「技艺」与「狡计」之义。

items.en: Middle English art could mean learning or craft, sometimes with a hint of trickery.
items.cn: 中古英语 art 可指学问、技艺，有时暗含「诡计」。

items.en: Artless appears in the sixteenth century meaning without craft or cunning.
items.cn: 十六世纪 artless 出现，意为无机巧、不狡诈。

items.en: Modern English keeps the honest sense and adds the clumsy, unskilled sense.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「天真」义，并发展出「笨拙」义。

note.en: Do not confuse artless with words built on the modern idea of fine art; the root here is craft and cunning.
note.cn: 不要把 artless 理解为「与美术无关」，其词根义是「技艺与诡计」，-less 表否定。

entries.definition: cunning and clever at achieving aims by trickery
entries.definitionCN: 狡猾的；巧于欺诈的（与 artless 同根反义）

entries.definition: in a cunning or skillful way
entries.definitionCN: 狡黠地；巧妙地

entries.definition: great artistic skill
entries.definitionCN: 艺术技巧；艺术功力

entries.definition: noun form meaning lack of cunning
entries.definitionCN: 天真；质朴（由 artless 派生的名词）

entries.definition: showing lack of experience and worldly wisdom
entries.definitionCN: 天真的；缺乏阅历的

entries.definition: innocent, honest, and direct
entries.definitionCN: 纯真的；坦率的

entries.definition: devoid of guile; honest and straightforward
entries.definitionCN: 不狡诈的；坦率的

entries.definition: plain and without pretense or complication
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的；单纯的

entries.definition: open and sincere in expression
entries.definitionCN: 坦率的；直言的

normalIntro.en: Break the word into art + less: without art, that is, without trickery.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 art + less：没有「心机」艺术，就是天真无邪。

normal.en: art once meant cunning; -less removes it.
normal.cn: art 古义为「诡计」，-less 把它去掉，即无机心。

normal.en: an artless remark is blunt and honest.
normal.cn: artless remark 是直率无心的话。

normal.en: artful is the exact opposite: full of tricks.
normal.cn: artful 恰是反义：满肚子花招。

normal.en: compare guileless, built the same way from guile.
normal.cn: 对比 guileless，由 guile（狡诈）同样方式构成。

normal.en: the clumsy sense grows from lacking skill or craft.
normal.cn: 「笨拙」义来自「缺乏技艺」。"

abstract.en: Picture a child's drawing with no correction marks.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅孩子的画，没有任何修改的痕迹——天真质朴。

abstract.en: Imagine a door with no lock: nothing hidden, nothing guarded.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有锁的门：无所隐藏，无所设防。

abstract.en: Feel the difference between a fencer's feint and an open hand.
abstract.cn: 体会剑客的虚晃与摊开的手掌之间的差别。

examples.en: Her artless honesty made everyone trust her at once.
examples.cn: 她不加掩饰的坦诚让大家立刻信任了她。

examples.en: The film's artless pacing was praised as refreshingly sincere.
examples.cn: 影片质朴无修饰的节奏被认为真诚得清新。

examples.en: His artless forgery fooled no one.
examples.cn: 他拙劣的伪造骗不了任何人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿特拉斯」扛天的人最无私——artless 谐音「阿特拉斯」，联想到毫无算计、坦荡天真。

root: 源自拉丁语 ars, artis（技艺、巧计）经古法语 art 进入英语，后接本族语否定后缀 -less，义为「无机巧的」。

sensesIntro.en: The core image of having no cunning grows into honesty, naturalness, and finally clumsiness.
sensesIntro.cn: 「无机心」这一核心意象先指向诚实坦率，再指向自然不造作，最后指向笨拙低效。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand with nothing hidden in it
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的手掌，里面什么也没藏

branches.en: honesty without deceit
branches.cn: 无欺的诚实

branches.en: natural unaffected style
branches.cn: 自然不做作的风格

branches.en: clumsiness from lacking craft
branches.cn: 因缺乏技艺而笨拙

branches.en: openness of manner
branches.cn: 态度上的坦诚开放

branches.en: plainness in execution
branches.cn: 表现上的朴素或拙劣

intro.en: The word family shows how art, once meaning craft and cunning, generates opposites with -less and -ful.
intro.cn: 词族展示 art（技艺、巧计）如何借助 -less 与 -ful 生成一对反义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars gave English a family of words about skill and craft.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ars 为英语提供了关于技艺的词族。

definition_zh: v. 使膨胀；肿胀；使扩张
definition_en: to swell or stretch outwards from internal pressure
core_image: 被越来越多空气撑得发亮的气球皮；用力时皮肤下凸起成绳的青筋；一只被填过平常刻度的袋子
scene: 气球皮被越来越多空气撑得发亮。 Gas distended the balloon until the skin shone.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：气体从内部把气球撑大，皮绷得发亮。

derivatives.zh: 膨胀；肿胀；腹胀
可膨胀的；可扩张的

senses.title: Swell from inside
senses.definition: to swell outwards because of pressure from inside
senses.definitionCN: （动词）因内部压力而向外撑大
senses.example: Gas distended the balloon until the skin shone.
senses.exampleCN: 气体把气球撑到皮发亮。
senses.why: A balloon skin pulled tight over more and more air.
senses.whyCN: 被越来越多空气撑得发亮的气球皮。

senses.title: Swelling of a body part
senses.definition: of a body part, to swell abnormally
senses.definitionCN: （动词）指身体部位异常鼓起

definition_zh: 暗指；间接提及；典故；引喻
definition_en: an indirect or passing reference to something, especially a literary or cultural work
core_image: 半句话点到为止，听者心里已经明白
scene: 演讲者只提了一句那次著名的远征。 Her speech made an allusion to a famous voyage.
sceneCN: 这里的 allusion 是「暗指、引喻」（第 1 个义项：不点名的间接提及）；句意是她的演讲暗引了一次著名的远航。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「暗指；间接提及」
由 allusion 加 -ive 构成，义为「暗指的；多用典故的」
形近同根词，义为「错觉；幻象」

senses.title: An indirect reference
senses.definition: a brief or passing reference made without naming its subject directly
senses.definitionCN: 不直接点名而简略提及的表述
senses.example: The essay makes an allusion to an old scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章影射了一桩旧丑闻。
senses.why: From alludere "to play with": the words toy around the thing instead of seizing it.
senses.whyCN: 源于 alludere「戏耍」：言语绕着目标打转而不直接抓住它。

senses.title: A literary or cultural reference
senses.definition: a reference to another text, myth, artwork, or historical event embedded in a work
senses.definitionCN: 作品中嵌入的对另一文本、神话、艺术作品或史实的指涉
senses.example: The novel is dense with biblical allusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说充满圣经典故。
senses.why: Indirection becomes art when a whole story is summoned by a phrase.
senses.whyCN: 当一句话唤起整个故事时，间接指涉便成了艺术。

senses.title: A tactful hint at the unmentionable
senses.titleCN: 对难言之事的委婉影射
senses.definition: a delicate reference to something embarrassing, secret, or taboo
senses.definitionCN: 对难堪、隐秘或禁忌之事的婉转提及
senses.example: Her remarks contained a sly allusion to his past.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话里暗藏对他过去的狡黠影射。
senses.why: Subjects too risky to name survive only by allusion.
senses.whyCN: 不能明说的话题只能以暗指的方式存活。

senses.title: An allusion as the act of alluding
senses.definition: the act or practice of alluding
senses.definitionCN: 进行暗指的行为或做法
senses.example: Constant allusion made the speech hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的用典让演讲难以跟上。
senses.why: The noun can name the practice, not only one instance.
senses.whyCN: 名词既可指一次实例，也可指这种做法本身。

senses.title: A false impression (illusion, cross-sense)
senses.titleCN: 与 illusion 混用的误例
senses.definition: in confused usage, a mistaken sense belonging to illusion, "a false perception"
senses.definitionCN: 混淆用法中误承 illusion 的义，「错误感知」
senses.example: Careful writers keep allusion apart from illusion.
senses.exampleCN: 严谨的作者把 allusion 与 illusion 区分开。
senses.why: The two words share a root in ludere and are commonly swapped in error.
senses.whyCN: 两词同出 ludere 词根，常被误换。

senses.title: A shared shorthand between intimates
senses.definition: a reference understood only by those who share the background
senses.definitionCN: 只有共享背景的人才能领会的指涉
senses.example: Their letters are full of private allusions.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的通信里满是私人暗语。
senses.why: Allusion works inside a closed circle of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 暗指只在封闭的知识圈子里生效。

senses.title: A source acknowledged indirectly
senses.definition: a passing reference acknowledging a source or predecessor without formal citation
senses.definitionCN: 不正式标注而顺带提及来源或前人
senses.example: The thesis contains a quiet allusion to earlier research.
senses.exampleCN: 论文中含蓄地提及了更早的研究。
senses.why: Scholarly courtesy can be paid with a light touch.
senses.whyCN: 学术上的致意也可以轻轻一笔完成。

senses.title: Allusions collectively as texture
senses.titleCN: 作为整体质地的典故层
senses.definition: allusions considered collectively as the woven texture of a work
senses.definitionCN: 作为作品编织质地的典故总体
senses.example: The poem's allusion gives it its depth.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的典故层赋予它深度。
senses.why: Many small references aggregate into a stylistic fabric.
senses.whyCN: 无数细小的指涉汇成风格的整体织物。

definition_zh: 潮差；高潮与低潮的水位差
definition_en: the vertical difference between the height of high water and the height of low water at a particular place
core_image: 一根水尺立在码头边，涨潮的刻痕与退潮的刻痕上下分开，两道痕之间的距离就是潮差
scene: 港口潮位站里，值班员对比今早与傍晚的水尺读数说， The tidal range here is over eight metres, among the largest in the world.
sceneCN: 这里 tidal range 指「同一地点高潮位与低潮位之间的垂直水位差」（第 1 个义项：潮差本身）；句意为：这里的潮差超过八米，是世界上最大的几处之一。

pos.zh: 潮差；高潮与低潮的水位差

derivatives.zh: 本短语的修饰成分，由「潮」加形容词后缀构成，18 世纪起用于潮汐写作
本短语的中心词，源自表示「一排、一行」的古法语词，语义由「排列」转为「两端之间的跨度」
由本短语的修饰成分加副词后缀构成：以潮汐的方式（修饰动词）

senses.title: The vertical difference itself
senses.definition: the vertical distance between the high-water mark and the low-water mark at one place, measured in metres or feet
senses.definitionCN: 同一地点高潮位标记与低潮位标记之间的垂直距离，以米或英尺计
senses.example: The tidal range here is over eight metres, among the largest in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的潮差超过八米，是世界上最大的几处之一。
senses.why: range already meant the distance between two limits, so joining it to tidal produces the interval between the two water marks rather than a single water level.
senses.whyCN: range 本来就指两个界限之间的距离，接上 tidal 之后，得到的就是两道水位标记之间的间隔，而不是某一个水位。

senses.title: The printed figure for a port
senses.titleCN: 潮汐表上某个港口的潮差数值
senses.definition: the number listed for a named port in tide tables or nautical charts
senses.definitionCN: 潮汐表或海图上为某个具名港口列出的那个数值
senses.example: The chart prints the tidal range for every port on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 海图上为沿岸每个港口都印出了潮差。
senses.why: a tide table needs one figure per place, and the phrase becomes the label on that printed line rather than the water it describes.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐表每个地点需要一个数，短语于是成了那一行印刷数字的标签，而不只是它所描述的水。

senses.title: The spring maximum
senses.definition: the enlarged difference at spring tides, when sun and moon pull in line
senses.definitionCN: 朔望时日月连成一线、引潮力叠加而形成的加大水位差
senses.example: Springs bring the largest tidal range of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 大潮带来一个月中最大的潮差。
senses.why: spring tides follow new and full moons, when the two pulls add, so the same measurement reaches its monthly maximum and needs its own qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 大潮出现在朔与望，两个引力相加，因此同一个量值达到月内最大，需要专门的限定语。

senses.title: The neap minimum
senses.definition: the reduced difference at neap tides, when the two pulls oppose each other
senses.definitionCN: 上下弦时日月引力相互抵消而形成的小幅水位差
senses.example: Neap tides give a tidal range barely half as large.
senses.exampleCN: 小潮的潮差大约只有一半。
senses.why: neap tides come when the sun and moon pull at right angles, so the range shrinks while the phrase keeps the same name with a smaller value.
senses.whyCN: 小潮出现在日月成直角相拉之时，潮差因而收缩，而短语仍用同一个名称，只是数值更小。

senses.title: The design average
senses.definition: the long-term mean difference used by engineers and pilots as a working datum
senses.definitionCN: 工程师与引航员作为工作基准使用的长期平均水位差
senses.example: Engineers size the sill from the mean tidal range.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师按平均潮差来确定门槛的高度。
senses.why: design needs an average rather than an extreme, so the phrase is qualified by mean and turns into a datum for construction.
senses.whyCN: 设计需要平均值而不是极值，短语因此加上「平均」这一限定，变成施工基准。

senses.title: The width of the bare shore
senses.titleCN: 潮差决定露出的滩面宽度
senses.definition: the horizontal extent of shore left bare at low water, as produced by the vertical range on a gentle beach
senses.definitionCN: 平缓海滩上由垂直潮差换算出的、退潮时露出的水平滩面宽度
senses.example: A wide tidal range bares a kilometre of mud at low water.
senses.exampleCN: 潮差大时，退潮会露出一公里宽的泥滩。
senses.why: the vertical difference maps onto horizontal distance because a gentle beach turns every metre of fall into many metres of shore.
senses.whyCN: 垂直差值会换算成水平距离，因为平缓海滩把每下降一米变成好几米的滩面。

senses.title: The head available for power
senses.definition: the water-level difference that a tidal power scheme can use to drive turbines
senses.definitionCN: 潮汐发电方案可用来驱动涡轮的水位差
senses.example: The plant's output rises with the tidal range.
senses.exampleCN: 这座电站的发电量随潮差增大而上升。
senses.why: a tidal plant runs on the head between high and low water, so the range stops being a description and becomes stored energy.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐电站靠高低潮之间的水头运转，潮差于是不再只是描述，而成了储存的能量。

senses.title: The effect of coastal shape
senses.titleCN: 海岸形状造成的潮差放大
senses.definition: the local value produced when the shape of a bay or funnel concentrates the incoming tide
senses.definitionCN: 海湾或漏斗形岸线汇聚涌来的潮水后形成的当地数值
senses.example: The funnel shape of the bay amplifies its tidal range.
senses.exampleCN: 海湾的漏斗形状放大了它的潮差。
senses.why: a narrowing funnel forces the same water into a smaller width, so the height grows and the local range becomes a signature of the coast's shape.
senses.whyCN: 收窄的漏斗把同样的水挤进更窄的宽度，高度因此增加，当地的潮差就成了岸形的签名。

senses.title: A record in sediment
senses.titleCN: 沉积层中记录的古代潮差
senses.definition: a past value reconstructed from old high-water deposits, used to trace sea-level change
senses.definitionCN: 从古代高潮沉积物中重建出的过往数值，用来追踪海平面变化
senses.example: Sediment layers record how the tidal range changed with sea level.
senses.exampleCN: 沉积层记录了潮差如何随海平面变化。
senses.why: mud keeps the position of old high-water marks, so the same interval can be measured in rock long after the water has gone.
senses.whyCN: 泥沙保存了古代高潮位的位置，因此水面早已退去之后，同一个间隔仍可在岩层中量出。

intro.en: Tidal range is a compound phrase, not a single derived word: tidal is tide plus -al, and range came into English from Old French range 'row, line'. The pair became a fixed term in nineteenth-century tide tables and charts. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tidal range 是复合短语，不是单一派生词：tidal 是 tide 加 -al，range 则由古法语 range「一排、一行」进入英语。这一组合在 19 世纪的潮汐表与海图中固定为术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tidal is tide plus the adjective suffix -al, formed when tide tables needed a word for the phenomenon itself rather than for one particular tide.
items.cn: tidal 是 tide 加形容词后缀 -al，形成于潮汐表需要一个指现象本身的词、而非某一次具体的潮之时。

items.en: Old French range meant 'row, line, rank', from the verb rangier 'to place in rows'; the noun first named things standing in a line.
items.cn: 古法语 range 意为「一排、一行、一列」，源自动词 rangier「排成行」；名词最初指排成一线的东西。

items.en: English took range in the fourteenth century; by the seventeenth it also meant the extent between two limits, as in a range of mountains or of prices.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 range；到 17 世纪，它又指两个界限之间的跨度，如山脉的走向范围或价格区间。

items.en: In nineteenth-century tide tables and sailing directions the two words were joined for the difference between high and low water, because two marks on a staff define an interval.
items.cn: 19 世纪的潮汐表与航路指南把这两个词连用，指高低潮之间的差值，因为水尺上的两道刻痕恰好界定一个间隔。

items.en: Twentieth-century oceanography qualified the phrase as mean, spring or neap range, turning it into a standard variable in charts, engineering and tidal power.
items.cn: 20 世纪的海洋学给这个短语加上「平均」「大潮」「小潮」等限定，使它成为海图、工程与潮汐发电中的标准变量。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the exact first citation of the phrase is not fixed, though the nineteenth-century dating is generally accepted; the Frankish *hring 'ring' sometimes proposed behind Old French rang is a reconstruction, and the ultimate origin of range is disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：该短语的最早书证没有确切年份，19 世纪的说法属于「一般认为是」；有人为古法语 rang 构拟法兰克语 *hring「环」，这属于重构，range 的更早来源本身有争议。

note.en: Group one holds the phrase's own parts and the other English words built on the same range root; group two holds neighbouring measures that are often mistaken for the range.
note.cn: 第一组是本短语自身的构件，以及建立在同一 range 词根上的其他英语词；第二组是常被误当作潮差的邻近量值。

entries.definition: the first element by itself: it means 'of the tide' and says nothing about a difference between two levels.
entries.definitionCN: 第一个构件单独使用：意为「潮汐的」，完全不涉及两个水位之间的差值。

entries.definition: the head noun alone means extent or scope of any kind; only the full phrase fixes it to water levels.
entries.definitionCN: 中心词单独使用时泛指任何范围或幅度；只有完整短语才把它锁定在水位上。

entries.definition: a- plus range, literally 'put into rows'; it keeps the original idea of lining things up.
entries.definitionCN: a- 加 range，字面是「排成行」；它保留了最初「把东西排成一线」的意思。

entries.definition: de- 'away from' plus range, 'put out of rows', hence to disorder or disturb.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 range，「把行列打乱」，因此指使混乱、扰乱。

entries.definition: the height of the tide measured from mean water to high water, which is half the tidal range.
entries.definitionCN: 从平均水位量到高潮位的高度，正好是潮差的一半。

entries.definition: the height of the water above a chart datum at a given moment, not a difference between two levels.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻水面高出海图基准面的高度，而不是两个水位之间的差。

entries.definition: the reference level from which heights are measured, usually low water; it is a baseline, not a range.
entries.definitionCN: 测量高度的参考面，通常取低潮面；它是基准，不是潮差。

entries.definition: the horizontal distance a water particle travels between flood and ebb; it is the range turned sideways.
entries.definitionCN: 一个水质点在涨潮与退潮之间水平移动的距离；可说是把潮差横过来量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two marks on a tide staff, one high and one low: range is the distance between two limits.
normal.cn: 水尺上两道刻痕，一高一低：range 就是两个界限之间的距离。

normal.en: The family runs tide, tidal, tidally, range, arrange, derange, ranger.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tide、tidal、tidally、range、arrange、derange、ranger。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical use: mean tidal range, spring tidal range, neap tidal range.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：平均潮差、大潮潮差、小潮潮差。

normal.en: Amplitude is half the range, and tidal height is measured from a datum.
normal.cn: 振幅是潮差的一半，而潮高是从基准面量起的。

normal.en: A funnel-shaped bay concentrates the tide, so the same ocean produces a bigger range there.
normal.cn: 漏斗形海湾会汇聚潮水，同样的外海在那里造出更大的潮差。

abstract.en: Picture a stone marked twice a day by the sea, and the gap between the two wet lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头被海一天标记两次，两条湿痕之间那道空隙。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens wider at the full moon and narrows at the quarter.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，满月时开得最宽，上下弦时收得最窄。

abstract.en: Picture a beach that doubles in width twice a day without moving an inch inland.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海滩一天两次宽度翻倍，海岸线却一寸也不向内陆移动。

examples.en: A tidal range of two metres shapes the whole beach.
examples.cn: 两米的潮差塑造了整片海滩。

examples.en: The bay's tidal range makes it a candidate for tidal power.
examples.cn: 这个海湾的潮差使它成为潮汐发电的候选地。

examples.en: Pilots check the tidal range before crossing the bar.
examples.cn: 引航员在越过拦门沙之前先查潮差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抬陡」加「范围」——潮水抬得陡，上下就拉出一个范围，这个范围就是潮差

root: tidal（古英语 tīd「时间、时辰」+ -al）+ range（古法语 range「一排、一行」，源自动词 rangier「排成行」，或出自法兰克语 *hring「环」的构拟）；19 世纪潮汐表与航路指南把两者连用，固定为「潮差」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow a single interval: the vertical gap itself, the figure printed for a port, its monthly maximum and minimum, the average engineers use, the shore it bares, the head it offers a turbine, the shape of coast that enlarges it, and the trace it leaves in sediment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都围绕同一个间隔：垂直落差本身、为港口印出的数值、月内的最大值与最小值、工程师用的平均值、它露出的滩面、它给涡轮的水头、放大它的岸形，以及它在沉积层里留下的痕迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two marks on one tide staff, one left by high water and one by low water, with the interval between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一根水尺上的两道刻痕，一道由高潮留下、一道由低潮留下，中间隔着一段距离。

branches.en: THE MEASURE ITSELF: first two marks on a staff, then the number printed for a named port.
branches.cn: 量值本身：先是水尺上的两道痕，然后是为某个港口印出的那个数。

branches.en: THE MONTHLY SWING: spring widens the interval, neap narrows it, and both keep the same name.
branches.cn: 月内的摆动：大潮把间隔拉大，小潮把它收紧，两者都沿用同一个名称。

branches.en: DESIGN AND POWER: the mean value sizes a sill, and the same head turns a turbine.
branches.cn: 设计与动力：平均值用来定门槛高度，同一个水头又推动涡轮。

branches.en: SHAPE OF THE COAST: a wide range bares a wide flat, and a funnel bay magnifies the range.
branches.cn: 海岸的形状：潮差大就露出宽滩，漏斗形海湾则把潮差放大。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: old high-water marks survive in mud, so the interval can be read in rock.
branches.cn: 深层时间：古代高潮位留在泥沙里，于是这个间隔可以在岩层中读出。

intro.en: This entry is a two-word phrase, so its parts are analysed separately: tidal is a Germanic root with a Latin-derived suffix, and range is a French borrowing with a Germanic reconstruction behind it.
intro.cn: 本条目是两个词的短语，因此把构件分开分析：tidal 是日耳曼词根加拉丁系后缀，range 则是法语借词，其背后还有一个日耳曼语的构拟形式。

latinIntro.en: Neither part has a Latin root: tide descends from Germanic *tīdiz, and range came through Old French from Frankish. Latin unda 'wave' and Latin latus 'wide' are unrelated words, so the Latin entries stay empty; only the suffix -alis is Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构件都没有拉丁词根：tide 出自日耳曼 *tīdiz，range 则经古法语来自法兰克语。拉丁 unda「波浪」与 latus「宽」都是不相干的词，因此拉丁条目留空；只有后缀 -alis 属于拉丁。

items.example: The tide kept the hour of the moon.
The same suffix builds tidal from tide.
items.exampleCN: 同一个后缀把 tide 构成 tidal。

items.example: Tidal water fills the harbour twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 潮水一天两次灌满港口。

items.meaning: row, line; later extent between limits
items.meaningCN: 一排、一行；后指界限之间的跨度
items.example: The range of prices surprised buyers.

items.structure: Old French rangier (verb, 'to place in rows')
items.example: Old French rangier meant to place things in rows.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 rangier 意为把东西排成行。

items.meaning: to put into rows, to order

items.example: The storm deranged the tide gauge.

items.meaning: a person who roams or guards a range
items.meaningCN: 巡行的人；管护一片区域的人
items.example: A ranger met us at the trailhead.
items.exampleCN: 一位巡护员在山道口接我们。

items.meaning: the interval between high and low water
items.meaningCN: 高低潮之间的水位间隔
items.example: The tidal range governs the harbour's schedule.
items.exampleCN: 潮差决定这个港口的时间表。

definition_zh: 浮空器；气球（靠浮力升空的飞行器）
definition_en: a lighter-than-air craft, such as a balloon or airship, that stays aloft by buoyancy
core_image: 一只系着缆绳的大气球静静悬在山谷上空
scene: 边境哨所的山顶上，一只系留气球白天黑夜悬着值班。 The aerostat hovered above the valley, tied by a long cable.
sceneCN: 这里 aerostat 是「浮空器」（第 1 个义项：靠浮力悬停的轻于空气的飞行器）；句意为浮空器拴着长缆悬在山谷上空。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「空气静力的；浮空的」
由 aerostatic 派生，义为「空气静力学」
历史用语，义为「浮空飞行术」

senses.title: Lighter-than-air craft
senses.definition: a balloon or airship that rises and stays aloft because its gas is lighter than air
senses.definitionCN: 因所充气体轻于空气而升起并悬停的气球或飞艇
senses.example: The aerostat hovered above the valley, tied by a long cable.
senses.exampleCN: 浮空器拴着长缆悬在山谷上空。
senses.why: Greek aer, 'air', plus statos, 'standing', names literally a craft that stands in air.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer（空气）加 statos（站立），字面就是「站在空气里的飞行器」。

senses.title: Ballooning as a practice
senses.definition: the art or practice of flying lighter-than-air craft
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶轻于空气飞行器的技艺或活动
senses.example: The museum traces the history of aerostat from Montgolfier onward.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展示了自孟格菲兄弟以来的浮空飞行史。
senses.why: The craft-name extends to the activity itself, as in older writers' aerostation.
senses.whyCN: 器物名扩展到活动本身，正如旧作家的 aerostation 一词。

intro.en: Aerostat comes from Greek aer, 'air', and statos, 'standing', coined in eighteenth-century French as aérostat.
intro.cn: aerostat 由希腊语 aer（空气）与 statos（站立）构成，十八世纪法语造出 aérostat。

items.en: The root *sta- meant 'to stand', and *wer- underlies the air word.
items.cn: 词根 *sta- 意为「站立」；「空气」词背后是 *wer-。

items.en: Aer meant 'air'; statos meant 'standing, set up'.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」；statos 意为「站立的」。

items.en: French coined aérostat in 1784, right after the first balloon flights.
items.cn: 1784 年，首次气球飞行后不久，法语造出 aérostat。

items.en: English aerostat named balloons before aeroplane took over the sky.
items.cn: 英语 aerostat 曾是气球的称呼，后来 aeroplane 主宰了天空。

items.en: The term now survives mainly for tethered surveillance balloons.
items.cn: 如今该词主要用于系留监视气球。

note.en: The first group gathers same-root craft words; the second gathers related flying machines.
note.cn: 第一组收同根的飞行器词；第二组收其他飞行器名称。

entries.definition: Particles in gas or a spray can; shares aero- but names a mist, not a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气溶胶；喷雾」；共享 aero- 但指雾而非飞行器。

entries.definition: The adjective of aerostat, describing buoyant flight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，aerostat 的形容词形式，义为「浮空的」。

entries.definition: At rest; shares the Greek statos root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「静止的」；共享希腊语 statos 词根。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a lighter-than-air craft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气球」，日常说法。

entries.definition: A steerable lighter-than-air craft with engines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞艇」，可操纵、带发动机。

entries.definition: A small nonrigid airship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「软式小飞艇」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the air-plus-standing root and the tether scene; the abstract hooks picture a balloon on a leash.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「空气加站立」词根与系留场景；抽象记忆点想象拴着绳的气球。

normal.en: Greek statos means 'standing'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 statos 意为「站立」。

normal.en: An aerostat stands in the air by buoyancy.
normal.cn: 浮空器靠浮力站在空气里。

normal.en: Aerostatic is its adjective.
normal.cn: aerostatic 是它的形容词。

normal.en: Tethered aerostats watch borders.
normal.cn: 系留浮空器用于边境监视。

normal.en: Aerostatics is the statics of buoyant air.
normal.cn: aerostatics 是研究空气浮力的静力学。

abstract.en: Picture a giant balloon held like a kite on a string.
abstract.cn: 想象一只被线拴住如风筝的大气球。

abstract.en: Picture gas straining upward against the cable.
abstract.cn: 想象气体向上挣、缆绳向下拽。

abstract.en: Picture an eye in the sky surveying all day.
abstract.cn: 想象整日巡视的天眼。

examples.en: The aerostat hovered above the valley, tied by a long cable.
examples.cn: 浮空器拴着长缆悬在山谷上空。

examples.en: Border patrols use radar-carrying aerostats.
examples.cn: 边境巡逻队使用搭载雷达的浮空器。

examples.en: Early aerostat flights thrilled all of Paris.
examples.cn: 早期浮空飞行让整个巴黎沸腾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「air »死搁」——气球「死搁」在天上不动，靠浮力一直悬停。

root: 希腊语 aer（空气）+ statos（站立）→ 法语 aérostat（1784）→ 英语 aerostat；核心义是「站在空气里的浮空之器」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the buoyant craft itself to the practice of flying such craft.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从靠浮力悬停的飞行器本身，扩展到驾驶这类飞行器的活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon that stands still in the sky on a leash
core.cn: 核心意象：拴着缆绳在空中静立的气球

branches.en: The craft that floats without engines.
branches.cn: 不用发动机也能漂浮的飞行器。

branches.en: The old art of flying balloons.
branches.cn: 驾驶气球这门古老的技艺。

branches.en: Both senses live on buoyancy, not thrust.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠浮力而非推力。

branches.en: Surveillance is its modern job.
branches.cn: 监视是它如今的工作。

branches.en: Montgolfier opened this chapter.
branches.cn: 孟格菲兄弟开启了这一章。

intro.en: The word joins the Greek air root aero- with the standing root -stat, and the family gives aerostatic and aerostatics.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语「空气」词根 aero- 与「站立」词根 -stat 组成，同族词有 aerostatic 与 aerostatics。

latinIntro.en: The combining parts are Greek; French aérostat is the recorded coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分来自希腊语；法语 aérostat 是有记录的造词。

definition_zh: 脱落；（植物器官的）自然脱落；切除
definition_en: the natural shedding of a plant part such as a leaf or fruit, or the act of cutting something off
core_image: 一片叶子在叶柄基部被一层细胞轻轻断开，随风落下
scene: 秋天一到，树叶基部形成一层特殊细胞，让叶片自然落下。 Leaf abscission begins when the days grow shorter.
sceneCN: 这里 abscission 是「（植物器官的）自然脱落」（第 1 个义项：植物主动断开并舍弃某部分）；句意为白昼变短时，叶片脱落开始。

pos.zh: 脱落；（植物）器官自然脱落

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「脱落；切断」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「脱落酸的；与脱落有关的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「脱落素」，脱落酸的旧称

senses.title: Shedding of plant parts
senses.definition: the natural dropping of leaves, fruits, flowers, or other plant parts
senses.definitionCN: 叶片、果实、花或其他植物部位的自然掉落
senses.example: Leaf abscission is controlled by plant hormones.
senses.exampleCN: 叶片脱落受植物激素控制。
senses.why: Latin abscindere meant 'to cut off'; the plant cuts its own leaf, and the word names that controlled separation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abscindere 意为「切掉」；植物自己把叶子切断，这个词命名了这种受控的分离。

senses.title: The fall of leaves
senses.definition: the seasonal process by which leaves are shed from a tree
senses.definitionCN: 树木按季节把叶子舍弃的过程
senses.example: Autumn abscission removes water‑losing leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季脱落会去掉会失水的叶子。
senses.why: Seasonal leaf fall is the most visible case of the plant cutting away a whole organ before winter.
senses.whyCN: 季节性落叶是植物在入冬前切掉整个器官最显眼的例子。

senses.title: The drop of fruit
senses.definition: the shedding of fruit before or after ripening
senses.definitionCN: 果实在成熟前后掉落
senses.example: Premature fruit abscission reduces the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 果实过早脱落会减少收成。
senses.why: Fruit is cut free at the stalk when the plant no longer supports it, so the same separation image applies.
senses.whyCN: 当植物不再供养果实时，果实就在果柄处被切离，因此同一个分离意象适用。

senses.title: Surgical removal
senses.definition: the removal of a part by cutting, especially in older medical writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过切割去除某部分，尤见于较早医学文献
senses.example: The older term abscission referred to cutting away tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的术语 abscission 指把组织切掉。
senses.why: Medicine used the literal sense first: tissue is cut off, exactly as the Latin verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 医学先使用这个字面义：组织被切掉，正如拉丁动词所描述的那样。

senses.title: The abscission zone
senses.definition: the layer of cells at the base of a plant part where separation occurs
senses.definitionCN: 植物器官基部发生分离的细胞层
senses.example: A visible line marks the abscission zone.
senses.exampleCN: 一条可见的线标出脱落区。
senses.why: The zone is the seam where the cut will happen, so the place of separation takes the name of the process.
senses.whyCN: 脱落区就是即将发生切断的接缝，于是分离的地点借用了过程的名字。

senses.title: Separation of flowers
senses.definition: the shedding of petals or whole flowers after pollination
senses.definitionCN: 授粉后花瓣或整朵花的掉落
senses.example: Flower abscission follows pollination in many species.
senses.exampleCN: 许多物种在授粉后发生花器官脱落。
senses.why: Once pollination is done, the flower's work is finished, and the plant cuts the now-useless parts away.
senses.whyCN: 授粉完成后，花的任务就结束了，植物便把不再有用的部分切掉。

senses.title: Cutting off in general
senses.definition: the act of cutting something away from its base
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从基部切离的行为
senses.example: The word abscission is rare outside botany and surgery.
senses.exampleCN: abscission 一词在植物学与外科之外很少使用。
senses.why: The general sense is simply the Latin verb translated: any cutting away from a base.
senses.whyCN: 一般义就是拉丁动词的直译：任何从基部切离的行为。

senses.title: A sharp separation
senses.definition: a sudden or clean separation of one thing from another
senses.definitionCN: 一物从另一物上突然或干净地分离
senses.example: The report describes the abscission of the ice shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了冰架的断裂分离。
senses.why: Large structures can also break along a seam, so the botanical image extends to ice and rock.
senses.whyCN: 大型结构也能沿接缝断开，因此植物学意象延伸到冰体与岩石。

intro.en: Abscission comes from a Latin noun for cutting off, built from a prefix and the verb for cutting.
intro.cn: abscission 来自一个意为「切掉」的拉丁语名词，由前缀与表示「切」的动词构成。

items.en: The root *skheID- is reconstructed with the sense 'to cut, split'; the exact reconstruction varies among sources.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *skheID- 被重构为「切、劈」之义；不同来源的具体重构形式不一致。

items.en: scindere meant 'to cut, split', and it also lies behind scissors and rescind.
items.cn: scindere 意为「切、劈」，scissors 与 rescind 也源自它。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus scindere formed abscindere, 'to cut off'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 scindere 构成 abscindere，意为「切掉」。

items.en: The noun abscissio named the act of cutting off, the direct source of English abscission.
items.cn: 名词 abscissio 指切掉的行为，是英语 abscission 的直接来源。

items.en: English abscission first appeared in medical and general writing for cutting away a part.
items.cn: 英语 abscission 最初出现在医学与一般文献中，指切去某部分。

items.en: Botany made the word central for the natural shedding of leaves and fruit, especially through the abscission zone.
items.cn: 植物学使这个词成为叶果自然脱落的核心术语，尤其通过「脱落区」的概念。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the acid adjective, and two other cutting words; the second gathers nouns for natural shedding and removal.
note.cn: 第一组收动词、酸的形容词与另外两个「切」词；第二组收表示自然脱落与去除的名词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to cut off or to be shed naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「切掉」或「自然脱落」。

entries.definition: An adjective used in abscisic acid, the hormone that controls shedding.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，用于 abscisic acid（脱落酸），即控制脱落的激素。

entries.definition: The horizontal coordinate in mathematics, literally 'a cut-off line'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「横坐标」，字面是「被切下的一段线」。

entries.definition: A cutting tool, from the same Latin verb scindere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剪刀」，来自同一个拉丁动词 scindere。

entries.definition: To cancel a law or agreement, literally to cut it away.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废除、取消」，字面是「把它切掉」。

entries.definition: The natural dropping of leaves, skin, or hair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脱落」，指叶、皮或毛发的自然掉落。

entries.definition: The state of becoming separate from something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分离、脱离」，指与某物分开的状态。

entries.definition: The act of taking something away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「去除、移除」，指把某物拿走的动作。

entries.definition: The surgical cutting out of a part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「切除」，指外科切去某部分。

entries.definition: The act of dividing or coming apart.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分离」，指分开或断离的行为。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the botanical collocations and the shared Latin cutting root; the abstract hooks picture the leaf's clean break.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用植物学搭配与共享的拉丁「切」词根；抽象记忆点想象叶片干净的断口。

normal.en: Leaf abscission and abscission zone are the core botanical phrases.
normal.cn: leaf abscission 与 abscission zone 是核心植物学短语。

normal.en: Abscisic acid is the hormone named after abscission.
normal.cn: abscisic acid（脱落酸）是以 abscission 命名的激素。

normal.en: Abscission and scissors share Latin scindere, 'to cut'.
normal.cn: abscission 与 scissors 共享拉丁语 scindere（切）。

normal.en: The verb is abscise, and the adjective abscisic belongs to the acid.
normal.cn: 动词是 abscise，形容词 abscisic 属于那种酸。

normal.en: In older medicine abscission meant cutting away tissue.
normal.cn: 在较早的医学中，abscission 指切去组织。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf stem developing a thin line of cells, then letting go.
abstract.cn: 想象叶柄长出一条薄薄的细胞线，然后松手。

abstract.en: Picture a fruit dropping onto grass while the branch stays intact.
abstract.cn: 想象果实落到草地上，而树枝完好无损。

abstract.en: Picture an ice shelf cracking along a clean seam and sliding away.
abstract.cn: 想象冰架沿一条干净的接缝裂开并滑走。

examples.en: Abscission protects trees from losing too much water.
examples.cn: 脱落能保护树木不过度失水。

examples.en: The abscission zone forms at the base of the leaf.
examples.cn: 脱落区在叶片基部形成。

examples.en: Fruit abscission can be triggered by stress.
examples.cn: 果实脱落可能由胁迫引发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布西申」——叶子基部像被小剪刀轻轻一剪，叶子就脱离枝条落下来。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ scindere（切），构成 abscindere（切掉），名词 abscissio；核心义是「沿一条线干净地切离」

sensesIntro.en: The senses center on the plant's controlled cutting away of leaves, fruit, and flowers, with extensions to surgery and clean separation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项围绕植物受控地切离叶片、果实与花，并延伸到外科切除与干净分离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf cut free along a thin seam of cells
core.cn: 核心意象：叶片沿一条薄细胞缝被切离

branches.en: Plant parts are shed in a controlled seasonal process.
branches.cn: 植物部位在受控的季节过程中脱落。

branches.en: The abscission zone is the anatomical seam where separation happens.
branches.cn: 脱落区是发生分离的解剖接缝。

branches.en: Older medicine used the word for cutting tissue away.
branches.cn: 较早的医学用这个词表示切去组织。

branches.en: The general sense is any cutting away from a base.
branches.cn: 一般义是从基部切离任何东西。

branches.en: Clean separation extends to ice shelves and other structures.
branches.cn: 干净分离延伸到冰架及其他结构。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem absciss-, the prefix ab-, and the endings -ion, -ize, and -ic.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 absciss-、前缀 ab-，以及后缀 -ion、-ize、-ic 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abscindere and abscissio are the direct source of abscission, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abscindere 与 abscissio 是 abscission 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其名词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「脱落；切断」
形容词，义为「脱落酸的；与脱落有关的」

core_image: 一条画在地上的线把人群分成两半，站在线下的人被逐一计数，比例写进表格
scene: 统计局把城乡家庭的收入逐户核对，再算出一条线以下的人占多少。 The poverty rate fell after the new benefit reached rural households.
