senses.title: Share below the poverty line
senses.titleCN: 低于贫困线的人口比例
senses.definition: the proportion of people whose household income is below the official poverty line
senses.definitionCN: 家庭收入低于官方贫困线的人所占比例
senses.example: The poverty rate rose when wages failed to keep up with rents.
senses.exampleCN: 当工资跟不上租金时，贫困率上升了。
senses.why: A rate is a fixed proportion, so the phrase first means the counted share of people under the line.
senses.whyCN: 比率就是固定的比例，因此这个词组首先指线下人口被计数后所占的份额。

senses.title: Official headcount ratio
senses.definition: the government's headline measure, computed by counting people below the line rather than by measuring the depth of their shortfall
senses.definitionCN: 政府的首要指标，按线下人数计算，而不衡量缺口深浅
senses.example: The official poverty rate ignores how far below the line some households fall.
senses.exampleCN: 官方贫困率不衡量有些家庭距线以下有多远。
senses.why: Counting heads is the simplest way to produce a rate, which is why the headcount version dominates official reports.
senses.whyCN: 数人头是得出比率最简单的办法，因此人头口径主导官方报告。

senses.title: Rate for a subgroup
senses.definition: the poverty rate calculated for one group such as children, older people or a region
senses.definitionCN: 针对儿童、老年人或某地区等单一群体计算的贫困率
senses.example: The child poverty rate is twice the rate for the population as a whole.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童贫困率是总人口贫困率的两倍。
senses.why: Any population can be divided into groups, and each group can have its own share below the line.
senses.whyCN: 任何人口都能分成群体，每个群体都可以有自己线下的比例。

senses.title: Rate before taxes and transfers
senses.definition: the share of people below the line when only market income is counted
senses.definitionCN: 只计算市场收入时线下人口所占比例
senses.example: The poverty rate before taxes is much higher than the rate after benefits.
senses.exampleCN: 税前贫困率远高于补贴后的贫困率。
senses.why: The order of counting matters: market income alone leaves out the effect of taxes and benefits.
senses.whyCN: 计数的次序很关键：只看市场收入，就漏掉税收与补贴的作用。

senses.title: Rate after taxes and transfers
senses.definition: the share of people below the line once taxes and benefits have changed their disposable income
senses.definitionCN: 税收与补贴改变可支配收入之后线下人口所占比例
senses.example: Benefits cut the poverty rate among pensioners by half.
senses.exampleCN: 补贴把领取养老金者的贫困率降低了一半。
senses.why: Redistribution changes the income that is compared with the line, so the same population can yield a much lower rate.
senses.whyCN: 再分配改变了与贫困线比较的收入，因此同一群人可以得出低得多的比率。

senses.title: Child poverty rate
senses.definition: the share of children living in households below the line, a widely used welfare indicator
senses.definitionCN: 生活在贫困线以下家庭的儿童所占比例，是广泛使用的福利指标
senses.example: The child poverty rate stayed high even as the overall rate fell.
senses.exampleCN: 即使总贫困率下降，儿童贫困率仍居高不下。
senses.why: Children cannot earn, so their rate reflects household income and is treated as a distinct policy measure.
senses.whyCN: 儿童不能挣钱，因此其比率反映家庭收入，被当作独立的政策指标。

senses.title: Internationally comparable rate
senses.definition: a rate adjusted to a common threshold so that countries can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 按共同门槛调整后使各国可以比较的比率
senses.example: Researchers compare the poverty rate across countries using a shared line.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者用一条共同的门槛比较各国贫困率。
senses.why: Comparison requires a common line and a common income definition, otherwise the rates are not the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要共同的门槛与收入定义，否则两个比率并不是同一回事。

senses.title: Disputed measurement choice
senses.definition: the rate as a subject of argument about line, income definition and treatment of benefits
senses.definitionCN: 围绕贫困线、收入定义与补贴处理方式产生争论的比率
senses.example: Two agencies published different poverty rates for the same year.
senses.exampleCN: 两个机构为同一年份公布了不同的贫困率。
senses.why: Because the rate depends on where the line is drawn and what counts as income, it is always open to methodological dispute.
senses.whyCN: 比率取决于线画在哪里、什么算收入，因此总会有方法上的争论。

intro.en: Poverty rate joins a Latin-derived noun for want with a Latin-derived noun for a fixed proportion. The compound belongs to modern social statistics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 贫困率由两个拉丁来源的名词组成：一个表示匮乏，一个表示固定比例。这个复合词属于现代社会统计。年代均为约数。

items.en: Rate comes from Latin rata (pars) 'a fixed portion', from reri 'to reckon', and entered English through Old French.
items.cn: 比率来自拉丁语 rata（pars）「固定的份额」，出自 reri「计算」，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Medieval use fixed rate as an assessed charge or proportion, the ancestor of the modern ratio sense.
items.cn: 中世纪用该词指核定的费用或比例，是现代「比率」义的祖先。

items.en: The poverty line was devised in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries as an income threshold for minimal needs.
items.cn: 贫困线在十九世纪与二十世纪初被设计出来，作为最低需要的收入门槛。

items.en: Poverty rate became common in twentieth-century social statistics as the share of people below that line.
items.cn: 贫困率在二十世纪社会统计中流行，指线下人口所占份额。

items.en: Governments adopted the rate as a headline indicator for welfare policy and international comparison.
items.cn: 各国政府把这个比率作为福利政策与国际比较的首要指标。

items.en: Attestation uncertain (first citation): the exact first use of the compound is unrecorded, and definitions of the line vary by country.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这一复合词的最早用例未被记录，贫困线的定义也因国而异。

note.en: Group one separates rates and ratios that are easily swapped; group two holds measures of poverty and count.
note.cn: 第一组区分容易互换的比率与比例；第二组是衡量贫穷与计数的词。

entries.definition: The poverty line is the income threshold itself; the poverty rate is the share of people below it.
entries.definitionCN: 贫困线是收入门槛本身；贫困率是线下人口所占比例。

entries.definition: The poverty gap measures how far incomes fall short of the line, while the rate counts how many people do.
entries.definitionCN: 贫困缺口衡量收入距线差多少，贫困率则数有多少人。

entries.definition: The historical poor rate was a local tax for relief of the poor, not a share of the population.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上的济贫税是用于救济穷人的地方税，不是人口比例。

entries.definition: Ratio is the general term for one quantity divided by another; rate is the fixed-proportion word used here.
entries.definitionCN: 比例是一个量除以另一个量的一般说法；比率在这里指固定的份额。

entries.definition: Incidence of poverty is the frequency with which poverty appears in a population, close to the headcount rate.
entries.definitionCN: 贫困发生率是贫困在人口中出现的频率，接近人头比率。

entries.definition: A deprivation index combines several lacks into one score instead of counting people below a single line.
entries.definitionCN: 匮乏指数把多项缺失合成一个分数，而不是按单一门槛数人头。

entries.definition: Headcount ratio is the technical name for the share of people below the line.
entries.definitionCN: 人头比率是线下人口所占比例的技术名称。

entries.definition: Poverty headcount is the raw number of poor people, from which a rate is then calculated.
entries.definitionCN: 贫困人头数是穷人的原始人数，比率由此算出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real statistical phrases and real distinctions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词部分、真实的统计说法与真实的区分。

normal.en: A rate is a fixed proportion, so the phrase always divides one group by a larger one.
normal.cn: 比率是固定份额，因此这个词组总是把一部分人除以全体。

normal.en: The line is the threshold; the rate is the share below it. Keeping the two apart prevents confusion.
normal.cn: 线是门槛，率是线下份额；把两者分开就不会混淆。

normal.en: Before and after benefits give two different rates for the same population.
normal.cn: 补贴前后，同一群人会得出两个不同的比率。

normal.en: The child rate is watched separately because children cannot earn their way out.
normal.cn: 儿童比率被单独关注，因为儿童无法靠挣钱脱困。

normal.en: Comparisons across countries need a shared line and a shared income definition.
normal.cn: 跨国比较需要共同的门槛与共同的收入定义。

abstract.en: Picture a line painted across a room and a person at the door counting who stands on the lower side.
abstract.cn: 想象房间里画了一条线，有人在门口数站在低侧的人。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer where the height of the mercury is the share, not the temperature.
abstract.cn: 想象一支温度计，水银高度表示的是比例，而不是温度。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of the same country shaded differently because the lines were drawn at different heights.
abstract.cn: 想象同一国家的两张地图，因为线画在不同高度而涂成不同深浅。

examples.en: The poverty rate among single-parent families remained above twenty percent.
examples.cn: 单亲家庭的贫困率仍在百分之二十以上。

examples.en: Official figures report the poverty rate before and after taxes.
examples.cn: 官方数字同时报告税前与税后的贫困率。

examples.en: A higher poverty line mechanically raises the measured poverty rate.
examples.cn: 提高贫困线会机械地抬高测得的贫困率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贫困」加「比率」——先画一条线，再算线下的人占多少，就是贫困率

root: 前半经古法语来自拉丁 paupertas「贫穷」，后半来自拉丁 rata（pars）「固定的份额」、出自 reri「计算」。两部分合起来，指低于贫困线者所占的固定比例。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one division: a line is drawn, people below it are counted, and that count is divided, subgrouped, adjusted for taxes, compared and finally disputed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次除法展开：画出线，数清线下的人，再做除法、分群体、调税收、作比较，最后引发争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on the floor, a counter at the door, and a table of percentages on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：地上的分界线、门口的计数人、墙上的百分比表格。

branches.en: THE SHARE: a count of people below the line is divided into a proportion.
branches.cn: 份额：线下人数被换算成一个比例。

branches.en: THE SUBGROUP: the same division is repeated for children and other groups.
branches.cn: 子群体：同一次除法在儿童与其他群体上重复。

branches.en: THE REDISTRIBUTIVE STEP: counting before and after taxes gives two different rates.
branches.cn: 再分配一步：税前与税后计数得出两个不同比率。

branches.en: THE SHARED LINE: comparison across countries needs one common threshold.
branches.cn: 共同线：跨国比较需要同一条门槛。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: because the line and income rules vary, the rate can always be disputed.
branches.cn: 争论：线与收入规则可变，比率因此总有争议。

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin noun for want with a Latin noun for a reckoned share, and both halves build common English words.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把拉丁语的「匮乏」与「计算出的份额」拼在一起，两部分都构成常见英语词。

latinIntro.en: Paupertas supplies the first half; rata and reri supply the second, with ratio as a close relative.
latinIntro.cn: paupertas 提供前半；rata 与 reri 提供后半，ratio 是近亲。

items.example: Poverty remains high in the region.
Poor households spend most of their income on rent.
items.exampleCN: 贫困家庭把大部分收入花在房租上。

items.example: The rate stayed near eight percent.
items.exampleCN: 该比率维持在百分之八左右。

items.example: The agency issued a credit rating.
items.exampleCN: 该机构发布了信用评级。

items.meaning: the relation of one quantity to another
items.example: The ratio of poor to rich widened.
Wartime rationing fixed each family's share.
items.exampleCN: 战时配给固定了每家的份额。

definition_zh: 无线的；无线电的；无线网络；无线设备
definition_en: using radio waves rather than wires to carry signals, or a system or device that works in this way
core_image: 屋顶上一根细天线对着天空，屋里桌面上没有一根线，音箱却在播放音乐
scene: 客厅的电视柜后没有一根多余的线，音箱和手柄都靠看不见的波与主机相连。 A wireless setup removes the tangle of cables behind the desk.
sceneCN: 这里指不用导线、靠无线电波传输信号的（第 1 个义项：无线的）；句意：无线方案省去了桌后缠成一团的线缆。

derivatives.zh: 复合词词干，古英语表示「金属线」的名词
由「线」的名词加已然词尾构成，义为「有线的、接线的」
由「布线」的动词加动作名词尾构成，义为「线路系统」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以无线方式」

senses.title: Carrying signals without wires
senses.definition: describing a system that sends or receives signals through the air rather than along cables
senses.definitionCN: 指通过空气而不是沿电缆发送或接收信号的系统
senses.example: The new headset is completely wireless.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新耳机完全是无线的。
senses.why: The word is the noun for a metal thread plus a suffix meaning without, so it literally describes what the system lacks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「金属线」的名词加表示「没有」的词尾构成，字面就描述了系统所缺少的东西。

senses.title: Radio communication as a field
senses.definition: the technology or practice of sending signals by radio waves
senses.definitionCN: 用无线电波发送信号的技术或实践
senses.example: Wireless began with telegraphy between ships.
senses.exampleCN: 无线电通信始于船舶之间的电报。
senses.why: Because early radio was simply communication without wires, the adjective became the name of the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 由于早期无线电就是「没有线的通信」，这个形容词便成了整个领域的名称。

senses.title: A local network without cables
senses.definition: a network, especially a local one, that devices join through radio links
senses.definitionCN: 设备通过无线电链路接入的网络，尤指局域网
senses.example: The cafe offers free wireless to its customers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆向顾客提供免费无线网络。
senses.why: A network is named by the medium that carries it, so the adjective alone can stand for the wireless network.
senses.whyCN: 网络以承载它的媒介命名，因此这个形容词单独使用就能指无线网络。

senses.title: A device that needs no cable
senses.definition: a device, such as a speaker or a mouse, that connects by radio
senses.definitionCN: 通过无线电连接的设备，如音箱或鼠标
senses.example: He bought a wireless speaker for the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他给厨房买了一个无线音箱。
senses.why: The adjective can shift to the noun it modifies, so the device itself is called wireless.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可以转指它所修饰的名词，因此设备本身就被称作无线的。

senses.title: Early telegraphy by radio
senses.definition: the historical service of sending coded messages by radio instead of cable
senses.definitionCN: 历史上通过无线电而非电缆发送编码信息的业务
senses.example: The ship's wireless operator stayed awake all night.
senses.exampleCN: 船上的无线电报务员整夜未眠。
senses.why: The noun form named the equipment and the service, a usage that survives in maritime and historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指设备与业务，这一用法在海事与历史写作中仍有留存。

senses.title: The technology of radio transmission
senses.definition: the engineering methods that move data through the air
senses.definitionCN: 让数据通过空气传输的工程方法
senses.example: Wireless research now focuses on low power and high density.
senses.exampleCN: 无线技术研究如今聚焦低功耗与高密度。
senses.why: A technology defined by the absence of wires is naturally named by that same absence.
senses.whyCN: 一项以「没有线」为特征的技术，自然就用这一特征命名。

senses.title: Audio without a cable
senses.definition: describing sound equipment that receives audio by radio
senses.definitionCN: 指通过无线电接收音频的声音设备
senses.example: The wireless earbuds pair with the phone in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 无线耳塞几秒内就与手机配对。
senses.why: Consumer audio adopted the word early, so the adjective became the ordinary label for cable-free sound gear.
senses.whyCN: 消费音频很早就采用这个词，因此它成了无线音频设备的日常标签。

senses.title: Free of physical ties
senses.definition: describing a situation in which no cable restricts movement or placement
senses.definitionCN: 指没有线缆限制移动或摆放的情形
senses.example: A wireless office lets people take the laptop anywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 无线办公室让人可以把笔记本电脑带到任何地方。
senses.why: The literal absence of wires extends to the freedom of movement that absence allows.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的「没有线」延伸到由此获得的移动自由。

intro.en: Wireless is a native English formation of wire plus the suffix -less, meaning without; radio gave it its modern sense in the 1890s.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族构词：名词「金属线」加表示「没有」的词尾；十九世纪九十年代无线电赋予它现代意义。

items.en: Wir named a thread of metal, and it is the same word English still uses for a conductor or a telegram.
items.cn: 古英语中这个词指金属细丝，至今仍用来指导线或电报。

items.en: The suffix means without or lacking, and it has formed English adjectives for many centuries.
items.cn: 这个词尾意为「没有、缺乏」，数百年来一直在构成英语形容词。

items.en: When messages were sent through the air instead of along a cable, the plain description wireless telegraphy was shortened to wireless.
items.cn: 当信息改为通过空气而非电缆传送时，原本的描述性说法被缩略为这个词。

items.en: Ship and coastal stations made the noun familiar, and the operator on board was called the wireless operator.
items.cn: 船舶与海岸电台让这个名词广为熟知，船上的报务员就被称为无线电报务员。

items.en: Broadcasting and later local computer networks extended the word from telegraphy to any cable-free link.
items.cn: 广播以及后来的本地计算机网络把这个词从电报扩展到任何无需线缆的链路。

items.en: The first published use of the shortened noun is generally placed in the 1890s, but the exact year and writer are not settled.
items.cn: 缩略名词的首次发表一般定在十九世纪九十年代，但确切年份与作者尚无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the wire idea; the second group names cable-free or radio-based alternatives.
note.cn: 第一组共享「线」这一概念；第二组是无需线缆或以无线电为基础的相邻说法。

entries.definition: Connected by cables; it is the direct contrast to the target word.
entries.definitionCN: 通过电缆连接的；是目标词的直接反义说法。

entries.definition: Describing cable-based telecom networks, used mainly in engineering and regulation.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以电缆为基础的电信网络，主要用于工程与监管语境。

entries.definition: A metal conductor; the thing the suffix removes from the target word.
entries.definitionCN: 金属导体；正是词尾从目标词中去掉的那个东西。

entries.definition: In a cable-free way; it modifies an action rather than describing a system.
entries.definitionCN: 以无需线缆的方式；修饰动作，而不是描述系统。

entries.definition: Without a cord, usually said of tools and phones powered by a battery.
entries.definitionCN: 没有软线，通常指用电池供电的工具与电话。

entries.definition: The medium of radio waves; it names the carrier that makes wireless possible.
entries.definitionCN: 无线电波这一媒介；命名的是使无线成为可能的载体。

entries.definition: Able to move or be moved; it stresses movement rather than the absence of cables.
entries.definitionCN: 能够移动或可被移动；强调移动，而不是没有线缆。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real native base, a real suffix and real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的英语本族词基、真实词尾与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Wire plus less: the word simply says without wire.

normal.cn: 同族词有线、有线的、布线、无线的与以无线方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the network: wireless network, wireless connection, wireless internet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出网络：无线网络、无线连接、无线互联网。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the device: wireless device, wireless speaker, wireless earbuds.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出设备：无线设备、无线音箱、无线耳塞。

normal.en: Ship radios made the word famous, and the wireless operator was a real job title.
normal.cn: 船用电台让这个词出名，无线电报务员曾是真实职位名。

abstract.en: Picture a kite whose string has been cut but which still answers a whistle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只风筝，线被剪断了，却仍能回应一声口哨。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every object can whisper to every other without touching.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，每件东西都能不接触地互相低语。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge made only of air, yet people cross it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座只由空气构成的桥，人们却能走过去。

examples.en: The wireless network covers the whole library.
examples.cn: 无线网络覆盖了整个图书馆。

examples.en: She prefers wireless headphones when she runs.
examples.cn: 她跑步时更喜欢用无线耳机。

examples.en: Early wireless operators worked through the night in stormy weather.
examples.cn: 早期的无线电报务员在暴风雨天气里通宵工作。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn one absence, no wires, into a medium, a field, a network, a device, a service, a technology, an audio label and a kind of freedom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个「没有线」变成一种媒介、一个领域、一张网络、一件设备、一项业务、一门技术、一个音频标签与一种自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signal travelling through the air where a cable used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：信号在原本该有线缆的地方穿过空气行进。

branches.en: THE DEFINING ABSENCE: a system that carries signals without cables.
branches.cn: 决定性缺失：不用线缆传输信号的系统。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS HISTORY: radio telegraphy, its operators, and the engineering that grew from it.
branches.cn: 领域及其历史：无线电电报、报务员，以及由此生长的工程技术。

branches.en: THE NETWORK: a local system whose members join through radio links.
branches.cn: 网络：成员通过无线电链路接入的本地系统。

branches.en: THE HARDWARE: speakers, earbuds, mice and other devices that need no cable.
branches.cn: 硬件：音箱、耳塞、鼠标等无需线缆的设备。

branches.en: THE FREEDOM: placement and movement no longer constrained by a cord.
branches.cn: 自由：摆放与移动不再受线缆约束。

items.example: A cordless drill is a close cousin of the target word.

senses.title: A snowstorm with violent wind

senses.definitionCN: 一下子涌来的极大量事物
senses.example: The office was hit by a blizzard of complaints.

intro.en: Blizzard is an American word of the early 1800s, and no origin has been proved; an older sense meant a violent blow.
intro.cn: blizzard 是十九世纪初的美国词，来源未获证实；较早义为猛烈的一击。

items.en: The word appears in American writing in the 1820s.
items.cn: 这个词在十九世纪二十年代见于美国文字。

items.en: An earlier dialect sense is a violent blow or volley.
items.cn: 较早的方言义为猛烈的一击或齐射。

items.en: It settles on the meaning of a wind-driven snowstorm.
items.cn: 它固定为强风卷雪的暴风雪之义。

items.en: The great storm popularises the word across the country.
items.cn: 一八八八年的大风暴使这个词在全国流行。

items.en: Weather services define a blizzard by wind speed and visibility.
items.cn: 气象部门以风速与能见度界定暴风雪。

items.en: Blizzard also means any sudden flood of requests or paper.
items.cn: 现代也指任何突然涌来的大量请求或文件。

entries.definition: A storm with heavy snow.

entries.definitionCN: 突起的猛烈阵风。

entries.definition: A violent storm, often in literature.

normalIntro.en: A blizzard is snow driven sideways so hard that the road disappears; the name sounds like a blow.

normal.en: The word is American and its origin is still unknown.
normal.cn: 这个词是美国英语，来源至今不明。

normal.en: An older dialect sense was a violent blow.
normal.cn: 较早的方言义是「猛烈一击」。

normal.en: Roads close, and the forecast warns before it comes.

normal.en: Paper can arrive like weather too.

abstract.en: A wall of white moving toward you.
abstract.cn: 朝你推来的一堵白墙。

abstract.en: A horizon removed in one night.
abstract.cn: 一夜之间被拿走的地平线。

abstract.en: Weather that behaves like a crowd.

examples.en: A blizzard shut the airport for two days.
examples.cn: 一场暴风雪使机场关闭两天。

examples.en: The new rules produced a blizzard of objections.

core.cn: 核心意象：横着抽来的雪，盖住了公路

branches.cn: 车灯在雪里什么也照不到。

senses.definition: the families who hold inherited title, land or privilege and pass it on
senses.definitionCN: 世袭持有头衔、土地或特权并传给后代的家族
senses.example: The old aristocracy kept its land through every change of regime.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老的贵族阶层历经每次政权更替都保住了土地。
senses.why: the Greek compound named rule by the 'best', and the class that claimed to be best became the word's centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊复合词本指「最优者」的统治，自称最优的那个阶层随后成了词的中心。

senses.title: Government by nobles
senses.definition: a constitutional form in which a small hereditary class holds political power
senses.definitionCN: 由少数世袭阶层掌握政治权力的政体形式
senses.example: Aristocracy was defended as a check on the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 贵族政治曾被辩护为对人群的制衡。
senses.why: the political sense is the original one, preserved in the -cracy ending.
senses.whyCN: 政治义是原本的义项，保存在 -cracy 后缀里。

senses.title: Rule by the best, in theory
senses.definition: the classical claim that the most capable should rule, whether or not by birth
senses.definitionCN: 古典主张：最有能力者应当统治，不论是否出于出身
senses.example: Aristocracy in theory need not be hereditary at all.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上的最优者统治根本不必是世袭的。
senses.why: aristos meant 'best', not 'well born', and philosophers kept that distinction alive.
senses.whyCN: aristos 意为「最优」，不是「出身好」，哲学家一直保留这一区分。

senses.title: Any privileged upper group
senses.titleCN: 任何一个特权上层集团
senses.definition: an advantaged group that closes ranks and reproduces its advantages
senses.definitionCN: 抱团并复制自身优势的有利群体
senses.example: The party became an aristocracy of its own founding families.
senses.exampleCN: 这个党变成了由创始家族构成的贵族层。
senses.why: the word travels to any group that behaves like a hereditary elite, even without titles.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有头衔，任何行为像世袭精英的群体也能被这个词覆盖。

senses.title: The privileges themselves
senses.definition: the exemptions, offices and advantages reserved for the class
senses.definitionCN: 专为该阶层保留的豁免、职位与好处
senses.example: Tax exemptions were the aristocracy's most durable privilege.
senses.exampleCN: 免税是贵族最持久的特权。
senses.why: metonymy lets the class stand for what it holds, and privileges were what it held.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让阶层代表它所持有之物，而它持有的正是特权。

senses.title: A country's nobles collectively
senses.definition: the noble families of one country taken as a single body
senses.definitionCN: 一国贵族家族被视为一个整体
senses.example: The English aristocracy married into trade for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 英国贵族与商界通婚长达两个世纪。
senses.why: national histories need one noun for the whole body, and this is the usual one.
senses.whyCN: 国别史需要一个词指整体，这通常就是那个词。

senses.title: A cultural elite
senses.definition: a group that dominates taste and standards without holding office
senses.definitionCN: 不掌权却主导品味与标准的群体
senses.example: Critics spoke of an aristocracy of taste.
senses.exampleCN: 批评家谈到一种品味上的贵族。
senses.why: authority over standards reproduces the old claim to be the best, minus the land.
senses.whyCN: 对标准的话语权复制了旧的「最优」主张，只是没有了土地。

senses.title: An entrenched elite
senses.definition: a closed circle that defends its position against newcomers
senses.definitionCN: 对外来者守门、维护自身地位的封闭圈子
senses.example: The university was called an aristocracy of examiners.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学被称作考官构成的贵族集团。
senses.why: the pejorative use keeps only the closure, which is what critics object to.
senses.whyCN: 贬义用法只留下封闭性，而批评者反对的正是封闭。

intro.en: Aristocracy comes from Greek aristokratia 'rule of the best', built on aristos 'best' and kratos 'power'. It entered English through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: aristocracy 来自希腊 aristokratia「最优者的统治」，由 aristos「最优」与 kratos「力量」构成。它经法语在 16 世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aristos meant 'best' and served as the superlative of agathos 'good'. Its formation is not fully explained; the older segmentation into a prefix and an unknown root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: aristos 意为「最优」，是 agathos「好」的最高级。其构成未获完整解释；把它切成前缀加未知词根的旧办法只是假说。

items.en: Kratos meant 'strength, might', and -kratia named a form of rule, as in democracy and oligarchy.
items.cn: kratos 意为「力量、强权」，-kratia 指某种统治形式，如民主制与寡头制。

items.en: Aristokratia named rule by the best citizens, a constitutional form discussed by Plato and Aristotle rather than a hereditary class.
items.cn: aristokratia 指最优公民的统治，是柏拉图与亚里士多德讨论的一种政体，而非世袭阶层。

items.en: French aristocratie passed the political term into English in the sixteenth century, still meaning a form of government.
items.cn: 法语 aristocratie 在 16 世纪把这个政治术语带入英语，当时仍指一种政体。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word commonly named the noble class itself, especially after that class lost direct rule.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，这个词常指贵族阶层本身，尤其在该阶层失去直接统治权之后。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the internal make-up of aristos is not established, and the pre-Greek origin of kratos is unsettled, so older forms offered for either are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：aristos 的内部构成未得到证明；kratos 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，为二者提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the -cracy or arist- stem; group two holds terms for ruling classes.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -cracy 或 arist- 词干；第二组是统治阶层的术语。

entries.definition: A single member of the class; aristocracy names the class or the form of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 该阶层的一员；aristocracy 指阶层或统治形式。

entries.definition: Describing noble origin or manner; it cannot stand for the class itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述贵族出身或风度；不能指阶层本身。

entries.definition: Autos 'self' plus kratos: rule by one person alone, sharing the suffix but not the claim to be best.
entries.definitionCN: autos「自身」加 kratos：一人独治，后缀相同，却没有「最优」的主张。

entries.definition: Rule by those judged most able, often coined as the opposite of inherited aristocracy.
entries.definitionCN: 由被认为最有能力者统治，常被造出来作为世袭贵族制的对立面。

entries.definition: The body of titled families, close to the first sense of aristocracy but without the claim about rule.
entries.definitionCN: 有头衔的家族总体，接近 aristocracy 的第一义，但不含统治主张。

entries.definition: The minor landed class below the nobility, especially in England; aristocracy can include them loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 贵族之下有地而无头衔的阶层，尤指英格兰；aristocracy 有时宽泛地包含他们。

entries.tag: few rulers no claim of best
entries.definition: Rule by a small group, defined by number rather than by virtue; aristocracy claims virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 由小集团统治，按人数而非德性定义；aristocracy 则自称德性。

entries.definition: The most advantaged group in any field; it is neutral about birth, which aristocracy is not.
entries.definitionCN: 任一领域中最占优势的群体；对出身中性，aristocracy 则不然。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aristos 'best' + kratos 'power': the best claiming the power.
normal.cn: aristos「最优」+ kratos「权力」：最优者主张权力。

normal.en: The family runs aristocrat, aristocracy, aristocratic, and the rival meritocracy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aristocrat、aristocracy、aristocratic，以及对手词 meritocracy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the class: the landed aristocracy, the old aristocracy, aristocracy of wealth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶层：有地贵族、旧贵族、财富贵族。

normal.en: Keep the suffix in view: democracy, autocracy, oligarchy, plutocracy all share -cracy.
normal.cn: 留意后缀：democracy、autocracy、oligarchy、plutocracy 都共享 -cracy。

normal.en: The Greek sense was a constitution, not a family tree; the class meaning came later.
normal.cn: 希腊义是一种政体，不是家谱；阶层义是后来才有的。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only to certain surnames.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，只对某些姓氏打开。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait gallery where every face resembles the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一间肖像廊，每张脸都像上一张。

abstract.en: Picture a claim to be best that nobody has to prove at the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一种「我们最优」的主张，在门口无需任何人证明。

examples.en: The landed aristocracy opposed the new inheritance tax.
examples.cn: 拥有土地的贵族反对新的遗产税。

examples.en: He argued that an aristocracy of talent is still an aristocracy.
examples.cn: 他主张，才能贵族仍然是一种贵族。

examples.en: Aristocracy survived the revolution better than the monarchy did.
examples.cn: 贵族阶层比君主制更经得住那场革命。

dict_mnemonic.text: aristo（最优）+ cracy（统治）＝ 自称最优者的统治；记「姓氏、土地、名帖」。

root: 希腊 aristokratia「最优者的统治」= aristos「最优」（其构成未获完整解释）+ kratos「力量」（希腊语之前的来源属重构形式）；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a constitution to a closed circle: the hereditary class, noble rule, the theoretical rule of the best, any privileged upper group, its privileges, one country's nobles, a cultural elite, and an entrenched circle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一种政体走到一个封闭圈子：世袭阶层、贵族统治、理论上的最优者统治、任何特权上层、其特权、一国贵族整体、文化精英，以及盘踞的圈子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house whose gatekeeper reads surnames before deciding which room to announce you to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座宅子，门房先看姓氏，再决定把你通报到哪间屋。

branches.en: THEORY AND OFFICE: rule by the best as a constitution, then as a philosophical claim.
branches.cn: 理论与职位：作为政体的最优者统治，再作为哲学主张。

branches.en: CLASS AND COUNTRY: one hereditary body, then a whole nation's nobles.
branches.cn: 阶层与国别：一个世袭群体，再是一国的全部贵族。

branches.en: THE SHAPE TRAVELS: any group that closes ranks can be called aristocratic.
branches.cn: 形状在迁移：任何抱团的群体都可被称作贵族式。

branches.en: WHAT IT HOLDS: privileges are what the class actually possesses.
branches.cn: 它持有什么：特权才是这个阶层实际握有的东西。

branches.en: WITHOUT LAND: taste and gatekeeping reproduce the claim in other fields.
branches.cn: 没有土地之后：品味与守门在其他领域复制了这一主张。

intro.en: Aristocracy joins a Greek superlative to a Greek noun of power, and both halves recur in English political words.
intro.cn: aristocracy 把希腊语最高级与希腊语「力量」名词接在一起，两半都反复出现在英语政治词中。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements reached English through Latin and French; kratos supplies -cracy, and aristos survives only in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊成分经拉丁语与法语进入英语；kratos 提供 -cracy，aristos 只存于这个词族。

items.example: Aristos names the best, not the well born.
items.exampleCN: aristos 指最优，而非出身好。

items.example: Kratos is the second half of many constitutions.
items.exampleCN: kratos 是许多政体词的后半。

items.example: Democracy and autocracy share this suffix.
items.exampleCN: democracy 与 autocracy 共享这个后缀。

items.meaning: a member of a ruling group
items.example: An aristocrat claims the first rank.
items.exampleCN: 贵族主张第一等的位置。

items.meaning: rule of the best; their class
a member of the noble class
items.example: The aristocrat refused the new title.
items.exampleCN: 那位贵族拒绝了新封号。

items.example: An aristocratic accent travels further than money.
items.exampleCN: 贵族口音比钱走得更远。
meritocracy 是为对抗 aristocracy 而造的。

definition_zh: 由相互连接的部件组成、共同传递力与运动的整套装置；也指力学分析中被一起处理的受力物体组合
definition_en: a set of connected parts that work together to carry force and motion, or the group of bodies treated together in a mechanics analysis
core_image: 齿轮、连杆与轴承咬合成一条传力路线，动力从输入轴进入，经各部件推到输出端
scene: 装配车间里，工程师转动输入轴，观察齿轮与连杆怎样把动力送到输出端。 The engineers tested the mechanical system before shipping it.
sceneCN: 这里指由齿轮、连杆等部件组成并共同传力的整套装置（第 1 个义项：由相互连接的部件组成、共同传递力与运动的整套装置）；句意：工程师在发货前测试了这套机械系统。

pos.zh: 机械系统；力学系统；机械装置

derivatives.zh: 由「机械的」这一形容词转成的名词，义为「机械师、修理工」
由「机械」的希腊语名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「机械的」
由「机械」词干加表示「结构、装置」的名词词尾构成，义为「机构、机理」
由「机械」词干加表示「使成为」的动词词尾构成，义为「使机械化」
由希腊语表示「一起放置」的词构成，义为「系统」
由「系统」加形容词词尾构成，义为「系统的、有条理的」
由「系统的」加动词词尾构成，义为「使系统化」

senses.title: A set of connected parts
senses.definition: an assembly of linked parts that transmits force or motion from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 由相互连接的部件组成、把力或运动从一处传到另一处的组合体
senses.example: The gearbox is only one part of the mechanical system.
senses.exampleCN: 齿轮箱只是这套机械系统的一部分。
senses.why: Mechanical names whatever works through physical parts, and system names an organized whole, so the phrase is a whole built out of parts.
senses.whyCN: 「机械」指靠实体部件运作的事物，「系统」指有组织的整体，因此这个词组就是由部件搭成的整体。

senses.title: Bodies treated together in mechanics
senses.titleCN: 力学中一起分析的受力物体
senses.definition: the group of bodies and forces that an analysis treats as one connected problem
senses.definitionCN: 力学分析中被当作一个连通的整体来处理的一群物体及其受力
senses.example: In the lab they treated the pulley and the hanging weight as one mechanical system.
senses.exampleCN: 在实验室里，他们把滑轮和悬挂的重物当成一个机械系统来处理。
senses.why: The phrase is borrowed from physics, where any chosen group of interacting bodies can be cut out of the world and studied as a system.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法借自物理学：任何一组相互作用的物体都可以从世界中划出来，作为一个系统来研究。

senses.title: A machine guided by sensors
senses.titleCN: 带传感器与控制的机械装置
senses.definition: a machine whose moving parts are monitored and corrected by sensors, actuators and a controller
senses.definitionCN: 由传感器、执行器与控制器监测并修正运动部件的机器
senses.example: The robot arm is a mechanical system guided by sensors.
senses.exampleCN: 这条机械臂是由传感器引导的机械系统。
senses.why: Once control hardware is added, the mechanical parts still carry the motion, so the old phrase now covers the whole controlled machine.
senses.whyCN: 加上控制硬件之后，运动的仍由机械部件承担，于是旧说法扩展为整台受控机器。

senses.title: The wheel train of a clock
senses.definition: the train of wheels and springs inside a watch or clock that turns the hands
senses.definitionCN: 钟表内部带动指针的轮系与发条
senses.example: A watch is a small mechanical system that has no battery.
senses.exampleCN: 机械表是一套不需要电池的小型机械系统。
senses.why: Before electronics, every timed device was a linked set of gears, and that literal picture survives in the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 在电子技术出现之前，所有计时装置都是连成一套的齿轮，这个词组保留了那幅字面画面。

senses.title: The drive line of a vehicle
senses.definition: the engine, clutch, gearbox and shaft that together send power to the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 把发动机的动力传到车轮的发动机、离合器、变速箱与传动轴组合
senses.example: The car's mechanical system includes the clutch and the driveshaft.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的机械系统包括离合器与传动轴。
senses.why: A drive line is exactly a chain of parts handing force along, so the general phrase settles on this familiar example.
senses.whyCN: 传动系正是一条逐级传递力的部件链，因此这个泛称自然落在这一常见例子上。

senses.title: The frame of a living body
senses.definition: the bones, joints and muscles of an animal viewed as a structure that carries load and produces motion
senses.definitionCN: 把动物的骨骼、关节与肌肉看作承重并产生运动的结构
senses.example: The bird's wing is a light mechanical system of bone and muscle.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟的翅膀是由骨骼与肌肉构成的轻巧机械系统。
senses.why: Because bones and muscles also form levers and linkages, biologists borrow the engineering phrase for living bodies.
senses.whyCN: 骨骼与肌肉同样构成杠杆与连杆，生物学家便借用了这个工程说法来描述活体。

senses.title: A rigid routine
senses.definition: an organization or process that repeats fixed steps without adapting to circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 不随情况调整、只重复固定步骤的组织或流程
senses.example: The old office ran like a mechanical system, with every form checked twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这个旧办公室运作得像一套机械系统，每张表格都要核对两遍。
senses.why: When people act without judgment, they are imagined as gears rather than thinkers, so the machine phrase becomes a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 当人不动判断地行事时，就被想象成齿轮而不是思考者，于是机械的说法变成了批评。

senses.title: Rule-bound logic in software
senses.titleCN: 按固定规则运作的程序逻辑
senses.definition: a module or procedure whose output is fully determined by its input and fixed rules
senses.definitionCN: 输出完全由输入与固定规则决定的模块或流程
senses.example: The billing module behaves as a mechanical system: the same input always gives the same output.
senses.exampleCN: 计费模块表现得像一套机械系统：相同的输入总是给出相同的输出。
senses.why: Programmers reuse the phrase for deterministic code, because such code follows rules the way gears follow teeth.
senses.whyCN: 程序员把这个说法用于确定性代码，因为这类代码遵守规则，就像齿轮咬合齿一样。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective for things that work by parts with a Greek-derived noun for an organized whole, and English engineers combined them in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词组把一个源自希腊语、表示「靠部件运作」的形容词，与一个同样源自希腊语、表示「有组织的整体」的名词拼在一起，英语工程界在十九世纪把它们固定成词组。

items.en: Mekhane meant a device, a contrivance or a means of getting something done, and it already carried the idea of parts arranged for a purpose; this Greek word is the direct source of the first half, while its still earlier root is a matter of reconstruction rather than settled fact.
items.cn: 这个希腊语名词指装置、巧计或达成目的的手段，本身已含「为某一目的而安排部件」的意思；它是前半的直接来源，其更早的词根属重构性质，尚无定论。

items.en: The derived adjective described what belongs to a device or is cleverly contrived, and it passed into Latin as mechanicus.
items.cn: 由它派生的形容词表示「属于装置的、精巧设计的」，并以「机械的」这一形式进入拉丁语。

items.en: Latin mechanicus kept the sense of something built or worked by physical means, and French and English took it over in the sense of machines.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留了「靠实体手段造成或运作」的含义，法语与英语随后以「机器」的意思接过这个词。

items.en: Systema meant a whole composed of several parts set together; it combines syn, meaning together, with histanai, meaning to set up or stand.
items.cn: 这个希腊语名词指由若干部分合在一起构成的整体，由表示「一起」的前缀与表示「安置、立起」的动词组合而成。

items.en: Late Latin systema and sixteenth-century English system kept the picture of parts standing together as one body.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语与十六世纪英语都保留了「各部分立在一起成为一个整体」的画面。

items.era: NINETEENTH CENTURY COMPOUND · FIRST RECORD DATE UNCERTAIN
items.en: As machine building became a science of linked parts, English joined mechanical to system for the whole assembly and for the body group that mechanics analyses; the exact year when the compound first appeared in print is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着机械制造成为研究部件连接的科学，英语把「机械的」与「系统」组合起来，既指整套装置，也指力学所分析的物体组合；该词组具体首见于何年并不确定。

note.en: The first group shares a word element with the target; the second group names nearby kinds of assembled equipment.
note.cn: 第一组与目标词共享构词成分；第二组是相邻的成套装备说法。

entries.definition: The working arrangement inside a device; it is the inner linkage, not the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 装置内部的运作机构；指内部连杆关系，而不是整套系统。

entries.definition: Worked by physical parts rather than by electricity or thought.
entries.definitionCN: 靠实体部件而非电力或思维运作的。

entries.definition: One powered device; a system may contain several machines.
entries.definitionCN: 单台动力装置；一套系统可能包含多台机器。

entries.definition: To replace human or animal work with machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用机器替代人力或畜力。

entries.definition: A group of parts put together; it stresses the putting together rather than the working whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把零件装成的组合体；强调组装动作，而非运作整体。

entries.definition: A set of equipment for a particular use, often in a lab; it stresses the equipment rather than linked motion.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途配置的一套器械，常见于实验室；强调器械本身，而非连动关系。

entries.definition: A temporary or improvised set of parts arranged for a test; it is rougher and less permanent than a system.
entries.definitionCN: 为试验临时搭起的一套部件；比系统更粗糙、更临时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Mechanical points to physical parts, and system points to an organized whole.
normal.cn: 「机械的」指向实体部件，「系统」指向有组织的整体。

normal.en: The family runs mechanism, mechanize, mechanical and mechanically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括机构、使机械化、机械的与机械地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: mechanical system design, mechanical system failure, mechanical system analysis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：机械系统设计、机械系统故障、机械系统分析。

normal.en: A clock is the smallest familiar example: wheels and springs turning hands.
normal.cn: 钟表是最小的熟悉例子：轮系与发条带动指针。

normal.en: A car drive line is the largest everyday example: engine, clutch, gearbox, shaft, wheels.
normal.cn: 汽车传动系是日常最大的例子：发动机、离合器、变速箱、传动轴、车轮。

abstract.en: Picture a row of hands passing a bucket along, each hand doing one fixed job.
abstract.cn: 想象一排手依次传递水桶，每只手只做一件固定的事。

abstract.en: Picture a locked staircase where every step must be trodden in the same order.
abstract.cn: 想象一道固定的楼梯，每一步都必须按同样顺序踩过。

abstract.en: Picture a company whose every form travels the same conveyor belt of desks.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司，每张表格都沿着同一条桌面传送带流转。

examples.en: The pump and the motor form one mechanical system on the test bench.
examples.cn: 泵与电机在试验台上构成一套机械系统。

examples.en: Students drew the pulley, the rope and the weight as a single mechanical system.
examples.cn: 学生们把滑轮、绳与重物画成一个机械系统。

examples.en: The factory floor is a mechanical system that still needs a human eye.
examples.cn: 车间是一套机械系统，但仍然需要人的眼睛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「机械」加「系统」——零件拼成一条传力链，环环相扣

root: 「机械」一词可追至希腊语表示「装置」的名词，该词更早的来源存疑；「系统」由希腊语「一起」与「安置」构成，两词经拉丁语进入英语，十九世纪合成词组。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: parts linked so that force passes through them. The parts may be gears, physical bodies, sensors, bones, or even fixed office steps.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个观念：部件连在一起，让力在其中通过。这些部件可以是齿轮、受力的物体、传感器、骨骼，甚至固定的办公步骤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of parts biting into one another so that motion entered at one end comes out at the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串部件彼此咬合，从一端输入的运动从另一端输出。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL CORE: an assembly of parts, and the same group treated as a problem in mechanics.
branches.cn: 实体核心：部件的组合体，以及被当作力学问题处理的同一组物体。

branches.en: THE CONTROLLED VERSION: sensors and actuators steer the moving parts.
branches.cn: 受控版本：传感器与执行器操纵运动部件。

branches.en: FAMILIAR EXAMPLES: the wheel train of a clock and the drive line of a car.
branches.cn: 熟悉的例子：钟表轮系与汽车传动系。

branches.en: THE LIVING VERSION: bones, joints and muscles acting as levers.
branches.cn: 活的版本：骨骼、关节与肌肉充当杠杆。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: people or code repeating fixed steps without judgment.
branches.cn: 比喻用法：人或代码不加判断地重复固定步骤。

intro.en: Both halves come from Greek through Latin; the adjective half carries the device root and the noun half carries the putting-together root.
intro.cn: 两半都经拉丁语来自希腊语：形容词一半带「装置」词根，名词一半带「一起安置」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied mechanicus and systema, both borrowed from Greek, so the Latin entries below are the forms English actually received.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「机械的」与「系统」两个借自希腊语的词形，下列拉丁词条就是英语实际接收的形式。

items.example: The Greek noun already implies parts arranged for a purpose.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词已含「为某目的安排部件」之意。

items.example: The adjective described cleverly built things.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述精巧造出的东西。

items.example: Latin passed the adjective to French and English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词传给了法语与英语。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective from a noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词词干变成形容词。

items.example: The noun joins a together-prefix with a verb of setting up.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把「一起」前缀与「安置」动词结合起来。

items.example: The prefix supplies the togetherness of the whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供整体的「共同」含义。

items.example: The verb supplies the standing of the parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供各部分的「立起」含义。

items.meaningCN: 由部分构成的有组织整体
items.example: English shortened the Latin borrowings into system.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁借词简化为「系统」。

items.example: The adjective is the first half of the target phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是目标词组的前半。
它把「机械的」变成「机械地」。

definition_zh: n. 下斜；倾斜；下坡（面）；渐降的坡度
definition_en: a downward slope or inclination, especially of the ground
core_image: 一条路从山口往下走，坡面一路朝低处倾下去
scene: 小路顺着草坡一路向下。 The path follows a gentle declivity.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：declivity 指向下的坡面；句意是小路顺着一道缓坡向下延伸。

pos.zh: 下斜；倾斜；下坡面；渐降的坡度

derivatives.zh: 陡峭下斜的
上坡；上斜
倾斜；倾向
下降；衰退

senses.title: A downward slope
senses.definition: a surface that slopes downwards
senses.definitionCN: 朝下倾斜的表面
senses.example: The path follows a gentle declivity.
senses.exampleCN: 小路顺着一道缓坡向下。
senses.why: Ground leaning away from the sky.
senses.whyCN: 地面向远离天空的方向倾去。

senses.title: The state of sloping down
senses.definition: the condition of being inclined downwards
senses.definitionCN: 向下倾斜的状态
senses.example: The declivity of the roof sheds rain fast.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶的下斜让雨水很快流走。
senses.why: A plane tipped so that water runs off.
senses.whyCN: 一个倾斜的平面让水流走。

senses.title: A gradual descent
senses.definition: a slow downward gradient in land or in a curve
senses.definitionCN: 土地或曲线上缓慢向下的坡度
senses.example: The road loses height in a long declivity.
senses.exampleCN: 公路在一段长长的下坡中降低高度。
senses.why: Height given up step by step.
senses.whyCN: 高度被一级一级交出去。

intro.en: Declivity comes from Latin declivitas, from declivis, sloping down, from de- plus clivus.
intro.cn: declivity 源自拉丁语 declivitas，来自 declivis（向下倾斜），由 de- 加 clivus（坡）构成。

items.en: Clivus meant a slope or a hill.
items.cn: clivus 意为坡或山丘。

items.en: Declivis meant sloping downwards.
items.cn: declivis 意为向下倾斜的。

items.en: Declivitas named the quality of sloping down.
items.cn: declivitas 指向下倾斜的性质。

items.en: Declivitie was an early English spelling.
items.cn: declivitie 是早期英语拼法。

items.en: Declivity entered English as a technical term.
items.cn: 十七世纪 declivity 作为术语进入英语。

items.en: Declivity was common in surveying and geology.
items.cn: 十九世纪 declivity 常见于测量与地质学。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cliv- slope root; the near-meaning group names downward gradients.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cliv-（坡）词根；近义组都是「向下的坡度」的说法。

entries.definition: A slope that goes upwards.
entries.definitionCN: 上坡。

entries.definition: A natural tendency to behave in a certain way.
entries.definitionCN: 癖性；倾向。

entries.definition: Sloping steeply downwards.
entries.definitionCN: 陡峭下斜的。

entries.definition: A surface that is higher at one end.
entries.definitionCN: 斜坡。

entries.definition: A downward movement or slope.
entries.definitionCN: 下降；下坡。

entries.definition: The steepness of a slope.
entries.definitionCN: 坡度。

entries.definition: A surface that slopes.
entries.definitionCN: 斜面。

normalIntro.cn: declivity 就是 de- 加 clivus（坡）：往下走的坡。

normal.en: Clivus means slope in Latin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 clivus 意为坡。

normal.en: De- points the slope down.
normal.cn: de- 把坡指向下方。

normal.en: Acclivity is the way up.
normal.cn: acclivity 是向上的坡。

normal.en: Declivity is the way down.

normal.en: Water runs down a declivity.
normal.cn: 水顺着 declivity 往下流。

examples.en: The village sits at the foot of a declivity.
examples.cn: 村子坐落在一处下坡的脚下。

examples.en: Cyclists slowed on the steep declivity.
examples.cn: 骑车的人在陡坡处放慢速度。

examples.en: The declivities here drain into one valley.
examples.cn: 这里的几道下坡都汇入同一个山谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: declivity 谐音「弟克利维提」——不如记 de（向下）＋ cliv（坡，与 acclivity 同根）＋ ity（名词）＝向下的坡，「下斜、倾斜」。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一块倾斜的地面：坡面、倾角与缓缓下降。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ground leaning away from the sky so everything runs down
core.cn: 核心意象：地面朝远离天空的方向倾去，万物顺势而下

branches.cn: 两者都是沿着地面走时土地在失去高度。

intro.en: Declivity is de- plus clivus plus -ity; the slope root builds up and down words.

latinIntro.en: Latin clivus means a slope and gradus means a step.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clivus 意为坡，gradus 意为台阶。

definition_zh: 易受……影响；对……敏感；可被……（处理或解释）
definition_en: to be likely to be affected or harmed by something, or to be open to a particular treatment or reading
core_image: 温室门口那排最嫩的幼苗最先垂叶，干冷的风一进门就先吹到它们
scene: 温室管理员发现，靠门那排幼苗最先垂叶，因为门口灌进来的干冷空气总是先扫到它们。 Seedlings near the door can be susceptible to sudden drafts of cold, dry air.
sceneCN: 这里指幼苗容易受到干冷气流伤害（第 1 个义项：易受疾病或伤害侵害）；句意为靠门的幼苗可能易受突然灌入的干冷气流影响。图中可辨识物件：温室、靠门的一排幼苗、垂下的叶片、半开的门。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）易受……影响；对……敏感；可被……

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「易感性」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「易受影响地」
由同一拉丁词干加另一形容词尾构成，义为「易于接受的」，较罕用
本短语的核心形容词，义为「易受影响的」
形近但不同源，出自另一个意为「从下往上看」的拉丁动词，义为「怀疑」

senses.title: Easily harmed by something
senses.definition: to be likely to catch an illness or take harm from a condition
senses.definitionCN: 指容易染上某种疾病或受到某种条件伤害
senses.example: People who sleep badly can be susceptible to every cold that passes through the office.
senses.exampleCN: 睡不好的人可能易受办公室里每一轮感冒的侵袭。
senses.why: Suscipere is to take up from below, so the word pictures a body that picks up whatever falls on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的本义是「从下面接住」，所以它画出的是一具把落下来的东西都接住的身体。

senses.title: Open to influence
senses.titleCN: 易受外界影响或被说服
senses.definition: to be easily moved by other people's opinions or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 指容易被别人的看法或压力带动
senses.example: Young readers can be susceptible to the tone of whoever speaks loudest.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻读者可能易受嗓门最大那个人的语气影响。
senses.why: Influence enters the same open hand: what is offered is taken up without much resistance.
senses.whyCN: 影响也落进同一只张开的手：递过来的东西没多少抵抗就被接住。

senses.title: Sensitive to small changes
senses.definition: to react strongly to slight shifts in conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指对条件的细微变动反应强烈
senses.example: The instrument can be susceptible to changes in temperature of less than one degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器可能对不足一度的温度变化也很敏感。
senses.why: Here the openness is to tiny differences, which is why the phrase suits instruments and organisms alike.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「敞开」对着极小的差别，所以仪器与生物都适用。

senses.title: Open to a solution or treatment
senses.definition: to be capable of being dealt with in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 指可以用某种特定方式加以处理
senses.example: The problem can be susceptible to a simple change in the order of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题也许可以通过调整步骤顺序来化解。
senses.why: Being open to treatment is the hopeful side of the same word: what can be affected can also be fixed.
senses.whyCN: 「可被处理」是同一个词里积极的一面：能受影响的东西也能被修好。

senses.title: Easily damaged by the environment
senses.definition: to corrode, crack or decay under ordinary conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指在普通条件下就容易腐蚀、开裂或老化
senses.example: Untreated metal can be susceptible to salt air along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 未经处理的金属在沿海可能易受盐雾腐蚀。
senses.why: Materials show the word at its plainest: no will, no mind, only an exposed surface.
senses.whyCN: 材料把这个词最本色的一面展示出来：没有意志、没有心思，只有暴露的表面。

senses.title: Easy to criticise or attack
senses.definition: to be an easy target for blame or argument
senses.definitionCN: 指容易成为责备或争论的目标
senses.example: Any plan that promises quick results can be susceptible to mockery when the first year is slow.
senses.exampleCN: 任何承诺速成的方案，在第一年进展缓慢时都可能易受嘲笑。
senses.why: The word turns from harm to reputation, but the structure is the same: an exposed side anyone can hit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从伤害转向名声，结构没变：露在外面的那一侧谁都能打。

senses.title: Open to interference
senses.definition: to be easily disturbed by outside signals or noise
senses.definitionCN: 指容易被外部信号或噪声扰乱
senses.example: A cheap receiver can be susceptible to interference from nearby power lines.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价接收机可能易受附近电线的干扰。
senses.why: Interference is just a draft in another medium, and the same open surface lets it in.
senses.whyCN: 干扰只是换了一种介质的气流，同一张敞开的表面照样放它进来。

senses.title: Open to a particular reading
senses.definition: to be capable of being understood in a stated way, usually with of
senses.definitionCN: 指能够被理解为某种意思，介词有时换成表示归属的那一个
senses.example: The old clause can be susceptible to two readings, and the court chose the narrower one.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧条款可以被读成两种意思，法庭选了较窄的那一种。
senses.why: This branch also admits a variant preposition of belonging, a small hinge on which legal usage turns.
senses.whyCN: 这一支还容许换用表示归属的介词，法律用法正是绕这一个小铰链转动。

intro.en: Susceptible comes from Latin susceptibilis, from suscipere, to take up or undertake, built on sub-, under, and capere, to take. English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century through scientific writing, where it meant capable of receiving an influence.
intro.cn: susceptible 出自拉丁语 susceptibilis，而后者来自 suscipere「承接、承担」，由 sub-「在下」与 capere「取」构成。英语十七世纪经科学写作借入这个形容词，当时意为「能够接受某种影响的」。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and it supplies a large family of capture, receive and accept words.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取、抓取，是 capture、receive、accept 这一大族词的共同来源。

items.en: Sub- plus capere gave suscipere, to take up from below, hence to undertake or receive.
items.cn: sub- 与 capere 合成 suscipere「从下面接住」，由此引申为承担、接受。

items.en: The adjective meant able to be taken up, and so able to receive an influence.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「能被接住的」，因此也就能接受某种影响。

items.en: English adopted it in scientific prose for bodies that readily receive disease or change.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪的科学文篇里采用它，指容易接受疾病或变化的身体。

items.en: To marks what harms or moves the subject; of marks a possible reading, and the distinction survives in formal usage.
items.cn: 介词 to 标示造成伤害或影响的东西；of 标示一种可能的解释，这个区别在正式用法里保留至今。

note.en: The first group shares the taking root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of weakness and openness.
note.cn: 第一组共享「取、接」词根；第二组是与「脆弱、敞开」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The state of being easily affected.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易受影响的状态。

entries.definition: Receptive or open to impressions, a rarer adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指易于接受印象的，较罕用。

entries.definition: To distrust or believe guilty, from a verb meaning to look up at.
entries.definitionCN: 指怀疑或有罪推定，出自意为「从下往上看」的动词。

entries.definition: To hang or stop temporarily, from a verb meaning to hang under.
entries.definitionCN: 指悬挂或暂停，出自意为「挂在下面」的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective at the centre of this phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 本短语的核心形容词。

entries.definition: Open to harm, often with a sense of needing protection.
entries.definitionCN: 指易受伤害，常带需要保护之意。

entries.definition: Likely to do or suffer something, often because of habit.
entries.definitionCN: 指易于做某事或遭某事，常因习惯所致。

entries.definition: Quick to react to small changes or signals.
entries.definitionCN: 指对小变化或信号反应迅速。

entries.definition: Willing to take in ideas or suggestions, a positive openness.
entries.definitionCN: 指愿意接受想法或建议，是积极的敞开。

entries.definition: Legally or commonly subject to something, often unpleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法律或惯例上易遭某事，多指不快的。

entries.definition: Available or exposed to a stated possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某种可能敞开或暴露。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the picture of taking up from below, the two prepositions, and the greenhouse where weakness shows first.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「从下面接住」的画面、两个介词的分别，以及最先显出脆弱的温室来记。

normal.en: Suscipere is to take up from below, so a susceptible thing catches whatever falls on it.
normal.cn: suscipere 是「从下面接住」，所以易受影响的东西会把落下来的都接住。

normal.en: Capere is to take, and the same root runs through capture, receive and accept.
normal.cn: capere 是「拿取」，capture、receive、accept 都同出这一词根。

normal.en: Use to for what harms you, and of for the reading a clause will bear.
normal.cn: 接有害之物用 to，接一种解释用 of。

normal.en: Vulnerable is the emotional cousin; susceptible is the neutral, technical one.
normal.cn: vulnerable 是带情绪的亲戚，susceptible 是中性、技术性的那个。

normal.en: A greenhouse door is the perfect picture: the weakest leaves sit where the draft enters.
normal.cn: 温室的门是最好的画面：最弱的叶子正好坐在进风口。

abstract.en: To be susceptible is to have a surface rather than a shell.
abstract.cn: 易受影响，等于只有表面而没有硬壳。

abstract.en: Anything open enough to receive a change is also open enough to receive a wound.
abstract.cn: 凡敞开到能接受变化的东西，也敞开到能接受伤口。

abstract.en: The same word serves the patient, the instrument and the argument, because all three can be moved from outside.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能用在病人、仪器与论证上，因为三者都能被外部推动。

examples.en: Young leaves can be susceptible to frost if the nights turn cold early.
examples.cn: 如果夜里提早转冷，嫩叶可能易受霜冻伤害。

examples.en: The alloy can be susceptible to corrosion in salt water.
examples.cn: 这种合金在盐水中可能易受腐蚀。

examples.en: The rule can be susceptible to a stricter reading than the one first offered.
examples.cn: 这条规则可以被读得比最初提出的更严格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 色塞普特波 图」——底下张开手，落下什么接什么：易受……影响

root: 拉丁语 suscipere「承接、承担」（sub-「在下」+ capere「取」）→ susceptibilis「能被接住的」；十七世纪进入英语。介词 to 接影响或伤害，of 接可能的解释。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe an open surface: harm, influence, small changes, treatment, material decay, criticism, interference and a possible reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一张敞开的表面：伤害、影响、细微变化、处理方式、材料老化、批评、干扰与一种解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the weakest seedlings stand where the cold draft enters the greenhouse.
core.cn: 核心意象：最嫩的幼苗正好站在冷风灌进温室的地方。

branches.en: THE OPEN HAND: whatever falls is taken up, including illness.
branches.cn: 张开的手：落下来的都被接住，疾病也在内。

branches.en: THE PUSH: other people's opinions enter through the same opening.
branches.cn: 推力：别人的看法从同一个开口进来。

branches.en: THE SMALL SHIFT AND THE SURFACE: tiny changes register, and untreated metal pays the price.
branches.cn: 微变与表面：细小变化会被记录，未处理的金属付出代价。

branches.en: THE FIX AND THE NOISE: what can be affected can be treated, and what is open can be disturbed.
branches.cn: 修复与噪声：能受影响就能被处理，敞开的也会被扰乱。

branches.en: THE TARGET AND THE CLAUSE: reputation is exposed, and a clause can bear two readings.
branches.cn: 靶子与条款：名声暴露在外，条款可以承受两种读法。

intro.en: The family turns on the Latin verb for taking, with a prefix of position and endings that mark possibility.
intro.cn: 这个词族围绕拉丁语「取」动词转动，位置前缀与表可能的词尾各司其职。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere and suscipere supply the core; sub-, -ible and -ity build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 与 suscipere 提供核心，sub-、-ible 与 -ity 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of capture and receive.
items.exampleCN: 它是 capture 与 receive 的根。

items.example: It gives suscipere its picture of catching from below.
items.exampleCN: 它给 suscipere 配上「从下面接住」的画面。

items.example: It is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It is the stem shared by susceptible and susceptibility.
items.exampleCN: 它是 susceptible 与 susceptibility 共用的词干。

items.example: It turns the stem into susceptible.

items.meaning: to look up at, hence distrust
items.example: It looks alike but comes from a verb of looking, not taking.
items.exampleCN: 它形近，却出自「看」的动词而非「取」。

definition_zh: 互利共生；互利主义；互惠互助
definition_en: a lasting association between two species in which each partner gains a net benefit, and by extension any doctrine or practice of reciprocal benefit between parties
core_image: 两株植物的根系在地下相互缠绕，一侧输出糖分、另一侧输出磷盐，两端都抽出新叶
scene: 这里指「互利共生」。 The fig and its pollinating wasp form a textbook mutualism in which neither species can reproduce without the other.
sceneCN: 这里 mutualism 指「互利共生」（第 1 个义项：双方都获得净收益的共生关系）；无花果与传粉榕小蜂构成教科书式的互利共生，彼此离开对方都无法繁殖。图中可辨识物件：榕果、小蜂、交织的根系、磷盐结晶。
